item.title: Pedri: Lamine Yamal shouldn't be compared to Lionel Messi
item.description: Pedri: Lamine Yamal shouldn't be compared to Lionel Messi Pedri believes Lamine Yamal should not be compared to anyone, insisting that measuring the youngster against Lionel Messi is "complicated" because it means comparing him to "the best player in history". The comparisons between Lamine and Messi have become a recurring theme, as the teenager continues to break records in Barcelona colours. Yamal’s ascent to, arguably, a status as the world’s best player has mirrored Messi’s own rise at the Camp Nou. Barcelona teammate Pedri is the latest high-profile figure to be asked about them. The Spaniard called comparisons with Messi an unfair burden, with the latter regarded by many as the greatest of all time. “For me, Lamine shouldn't be compared to anyone because comparing him to Leo Messi is complicated… …comparing yourself to the best player in history is complicated.” - Pedri "The best player in the world" That does not mean Pedri held back on his praise. At the same time, he labelled Yamal as football’s current number one. Pedri is not alone in pushing back on the Messi comparison. Earlier in the day, Paris Saint-German head coach Luis Enrique rejected it too. Enrique, who coached Messi during his time as Barcelona boss, will come face-to-face with Yamal when PSG take on the Spanish champions in the Champions League this evening. At his pre-match press conference, he talked down the comparisons. “Lamine-Messi comparisons? You can not compare any player with Messi, he's the best ever.” - Luis Enrique Yamal has started the season in exceptional form, with eight goals and six assists in just nine La Liga appearances. In Europe, he’s been similarly devastating. Yamal has recorded a goal and four assists in only 180 minutes of Champions League football. The teenager is a contender for the Ballon d’Or when it is announced this month, and could become the youngest-ever winner of the award, after a runners-up finish in 2025.

item.title: NFL fans hit out at one of the ‘worst national anthems ever’ as Grammy winner invites son to MNF
item.description: Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images Pat Monahan of Train made an appearance at the Monday Night Football game between the San Francisco 49ers and the Washington Commanders this week. The 49ers headed into the game still undefeated. In turn, it was perhaps not too surprising that they came away with a 23-17 win on the night. But while San Francisco’s start to the season has been impressive, much of the talk on social media about the game has focused on Monahan performing the national anthem with his son pre-game. Fans hit out after Train’s Pat Monahan and his son performed the national anthem at 49ers vs Commanders game Train, a band from San Francisco, have won multiple awards during their career, including picking up Grammys for ‘Best Rock Song’, ‘Best Instrumental Arrangement Accompanying Vocalist(s)’ and ‘Best Pop Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals’. However, a number of fans were not too keen on Monahan and his son’s version of the national anthem at the 49ers game. One fan wrote: “What in the world was that? Easily the worst national anthem ever!” A second stated: “Maybe THE worst national anthem I’ve ever heard. Good grief. Who booked this? You’re FIRED!.” Another echoed: “As someone who was around for Carl Lewis and Roseanne… that might have been the worst rendition of the National Anthem I’ve ever heard.” “Anyone else watching MNF was that the worst national anthem rendition you’ve ever seen?” asked a fourth. A fifth stated: “That was probably the worst rendition of the national anthem I’ve ever heard. Yikes.” Another added: “Worst national anthem I’ve ever heard and I was subjected to the 2024 home run derby debacle in person!” And a seventh stated: “That was the worst rendition of the national anthem I’ve ever heard,” while tagging the 49ers’ X account. It was also called a ‘historically bad performance’ by another account who shared a clip of it happening. Still, 49ers fans won’t much care as their team are now 6-0 after another solid display. Read more: NFL Network analyst apologises to Jalen Hurts after controversial comments over missing 2026 season ESPN’s efforts to change Jason Kelce look to have failed after ‘epic’ Monday Night Football moment Washington Commanders loss makes NFL history as NFC East sets embarrassing record

item.title: Camera catches Stephen Curry shouting message to Gabby Williams after Valkyries’ Game 2 loss
item.description: David Gonzales-Imagn Images Camera catches Stephen Curry shouting message to Gabby Williams after Valkyries’ Game 2 loss appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Golden State Valkyries failed to protect their home turf in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals , losing to the Atlanta Dream, 79-65, at Chase Center on Monday. The best-of-seven series is tied at 1-1. The Valkyries dug themselves a 21-point hole, which proved to be too much of a deficit to overcome despite a strong rally in the fourth quarter. As Golden State was walking off the court dejectedly, the camera caught Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry trying to cheer up Valkyries forward Gabby Williams . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Here we go, Gabby!” screamed Curry. Steph Curry cheering on the Valkyries despite the loss: “Here we go, Gabby!” 🐐👏 pic.twitter.com/E7ggDJfKUG — aly ✶ (@jinthirty) October 20, 2026 Williams finished with 14 points, two rebounds, and four steals in 27 minutes. She struggled from the field, shooting 3-of-15. She also had four turnovers. The two-time All-Star was coming off a heroic performance in Game 1, tallying 26 points, four rebounds, and two assists. Curry’s encouraging remark should help ease some of the pain after Game 2. He has been an ardent supporter of the Valkyries since the team was founded last year, including repeatedly touting Williams. The 30-year-old forward grabbed attention before the WNBA Finals for calling out the media . “The media’s never respected me. I’ve never expected them to. So that’s always been in the back of my head. I’ve never paid any mind to the media, so if the media’s praising me now, I don’t care,” said the three-time All-Defense. Tiffany Hayes contributed 14 points, two rebounds, and three assists off the bench in Game 2, while Veronica Burton had 11 points, seven rebounds, two assists, and two steals. Kayla Thornton and Cecilia Zandalasini combined for only seven points on 2-of-11 field goals. Game 3 is at State Farm Arena on Wednesday. Related: Stephen Curry, Yaxel Lendeborg catch Valkyries-Dream Game 2 before opening night Related: Angel Reese reveals Dream’s adjustments after letting Game 1 ‘slip away’

item.title: 'Forever grateful': Rohit Sharma thanks Dilip Vengsarkar for selecting him in Indian team for the first time
item.description: 'Forever grateful': Rohit Sharma thanks Dilip Vengsarkar for selecting him in Indian team for the first time originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: India 's batting legend Rohit Sharma has thanked former selection committee chairman Dilip Vengsarkar for picking him for the national team in 2007. Rohit Sharma said that without Dilip Vengsarkar, he might never have got the chance to play for India. Rohit Sharma also credited his Mumbai age-group coach Vasoo Paranjape for helping him earlier in his career. How Dilip Vengsarkar's selection started Rohit Sharma's India career Rohit Sharma's international career has now run for more than 19 years, and for much of this year the talk around him has been about when it will end. He has chosen to look back at the beginning instead and to name the people who helped him get there. Rohit made his India debut in an ODI against Ireland in Belfast on June 23, 2007, in a rain-affected nine-wicket win. He was only 20 at the time, and Dilip Vengsarkar, the former India captain, was chairman of the selection committee that picked him. The two people Rohit chose to thank belong to different stages of his rise. Vengsarkar gave him the chance at the national level, while Vasoo Paranjape, the veteran coach who died in 2021, had worked with him in Mumbai's age-group cricket before that. MORE: ‘(Rohit Sharma) wants that cup’: How Ojha’s appointment is good news for Indian veteran batter Rohit Sharma credits Dilip Vengsarkar for his first India selection Rohit was asked on his show , Family Full House with Rohit Sharma on Sony TV, “Who spotted you for Team India?” He began by saying, “That's an excellent question. Actually, quite a few people played a role in it.” Vengsarkar was the first name he mentioned. #RohitSharma credits former India captain Dilip Vengsarkar, who was the national selection committe chairman in 2007, and Vasoo Paranjape sir, for his selection into the Indian team in June 2007, on his show on Sony TV!! pic.twitter.com/XOOSAtEWPX — Gaurav Gupta (@toi_gauravG) October 20, 2026 Rohit then explained how the selection came about, and he made clear who had backed him at the highest level. He said, “When I was selected for the Indian team, Dilip Vengsarkar was the chairman of the selection committee, and he gave me the opportunity.” Rohit said the decision still means a great deal to him, since it opened a door that might otherwise have stayed shut. item.title: Wow, Andoni Iraola now wants Spanish superstar to join Liverpool
item.description: Wow, Andoni Iraola now wants Spanish superstar to join Liverpool Andoni Iraola has requested Liverpool to sign an exciting Spanish midfielder. Julian Ward has ushered in Liverpool’s new era without making too much noise. There has been no grand announcement or big fanfare surrounding his return to the sporting director role. Instead, there is a sense of uncertainty around Anfield, with supporters still trying to figure out exactly where the club is heading. At the moment, nobody really knows what the plan is. Will Ward continue building on the foundations Richard Hughes laid down, or will he look to take Liverpool in a completely different direction? That could even mean making some difficult decisions over players Hughes brought to the club, with Florian Wirtz potentially among those under the spotlight. Could Liverpool actually replace Wirtz? It would certainly be a bold move, especially considering the money Liverpool invested in the German. But football is a ruthless business, and sometimes you have to accept that things haven't worked out as planned. The truth is that it's probably not the club's priority. Liverpool's recent recruitment has left plenty to be desired. The club have spent enormous sums of money, yet there are still glaring holes in the squad and questions over whether certain signings are the right fit. That's not sustainable, and Ward needs to find a way to address those problems. The Reds cannot keep throwing more than £100m at individual players and hoping they arrive as the finished article. Recruitment has to be smarter, more strategic and focused on building a balanced squad rather than simply chasing the biggest names. Why Andoni Iraola wants Fermin Lopez at Liverpool Ward has an opportunity to reset things at Anfield. Supporters will want to see a clear vision, better recruitment and a squad that actually makes sense. Whatever direction he chooses, something has to change. Liverpool simply cannot afford to keep making the same expensive mistakes. Of course, Iraola is going to have his say as well. According to El Nacional in Spain , the Liverpool head-coach has already made a request. He wants Liverpool to sign Fermin Lopez. The report claims it would take €140m for Barcelona to accept an offer for Lopez and that Iraola has lost patience with Wirtz and is convinced the Spanish international would settle a lot easier at Liverpool. All of this is interesting. However, surely spending another £100m to replace a £100m player who hasn't worked out is not the wisest way to splash the cash?

item.title: 'Let's see where I stop!' - Bayer Leverkusen striker Patrik Schick proud after writing Bundesliga history with six-game goalscoring run
item.description: FBL-GER-BUNDESLIGA-LEVERKUSEN-FREIBURG - AFP Deadly frontman sets new benchmark Schick has expressed his pride after making German top-flight history by finding the net across each of the opening six matchdays of the 2026-27 campaign. The 30-year-old frontman sealed a 2-1 victory for Die Werkself against previously unbeaten Freiburg with a 76th-minute finish from young midfielder Ibrahim Maza's cut-back. His six-game scoring streak surpasses the previous club benchmark of five set by Dimitar Berbatov in 2005-06 and Stefan Kiessling in 2009-10. SIX IN SIX! PATRIK'S DONE IT! HISTORY MAKER! 🔥🔥 76' | 2-1 | #B04SCF pic.twitter.com/YQZDb7wjDS — Bayer 04 Leverkusen (@bayer04_en) October 18, 2026 Prolific striker relishes historic milestone Prolific striker relishes historic milestone That landmark feat builds on another personal milestone achieved earlier this term, when the forward became the club's highest-scoring non-German player in Bundesliga history. Reacting to his record-breaking run after the final whistle against Freiburg, Schick said: "Of course [the record] makes me proud. Six in a row, it's very nice. I'm lucky that I keep scoring and I will continue like that. Let's see where I stop!" Fitness recovery fuels title charge Enjoying the most prolific start to a league season of his career is particularly remarkable given how persistent injury setbacks had severely interrupted his previous campaigns in Germany. Now fully fit and firing, the attacker looks well capable of challenging his personal best of 24 league goals, achieved during the 2021-22 season. Beyond individual accolades, Sunday's result continued Die Werkself's impressive recovery under manager Carles Martinez Novell following an opening-day defeat to Elversberg, taking their recent haul to 13 points from a possible 15. Level on points with Freiburg in fourth place , Leverkusen sit just a single point adrift of leaders Bayern, firmly cementing their credentials as genuine title contenders. Away test awaits resurgent contenders Away test awaits resurgent contenders Leverkusen will now look to maintain their upward trajectory when they travel to face Hoffenheim on Matchday 7 . With their talismanic striker operating at peak fitness, the visitors have a prime opportunity to stretch his scoring sequence to a seventh straight league outing. Securing maximum points on the road will be vital for Die Werkself to keep the pressure on Bayern at the Bundesliga summit.

item.title: Judge in Larry Nassar abuse case says gymnastics still failing athletes amid calls for change
item.description: The judge who sentenced USA Gymnastics doctor Larry Nassar to up to 175 years in prison for sexual abuse has said the sport is still failing athletes in “almost every way” a decade on from the case. Judge Rosemarie Aquilina said reforms introduced since his prolific offending against more than 250 women and girls was exposed largely amounted to “window dressing” and said athletes remained afraid to speak out because of the possible consequences. She told Reuters : “I think that what they've done across the world is window dressing to say, ‘Look at us, look what we've done so well’, and they're still not being accountable for the things that they're not doing. “Safety is a human right and yet these athletes still feel that they don't have it because the sport they love will go away if they complain about anything and so we haven't come far ⁠enough at all. “I don't think we're going to see a change in my lifetime. I think it's going to take decades.” World Gymnastics and USA Gymnastics were not immediately available to comment. Aquilina was speaking at an event organised by Gymnasts for Change International in Rotterdam, where the World Championships are being held this week, to assess progress made on athlete welfare since Nassar was sentenced in 2018. Kim Shore of Gymnasts for Change Canada credited the sport’s governing body World Gymnastics for the positive progress made, but highlighted the wide variation in the sport around the world and the challenge of implementing reforms and safeguards at every level, including grassroots gymnastics. She said: “What we still consistently hear is that there's very much a control dominance style of coaching that is pervasive in the sport, which means that gymnasts don't have a strong voice. “There's still yelling, training on injuries, body shaming, preoccupation with thinness.” Shore said one encouraging shift was that athletes were increasingly staying in the sport beyond their teenage years, with gymnasts competing into their late 20s and some returning after having children. The discussion took place as World Gymnastics prepares to appoint ‌a new secretary general in the coming months, with Swiss Nicolas Buompane stepping down at the end of 2026. Minky Worden of Human Rights Watch said progress had been made in the processes for athletes to report abuse but said the new leadership should prioritise gymnasts’ health and welfare over silverware. She said: “Now I think there are better, not perfect, reporting systems in place... I think there are whistleblower protections, and there is a more trauma-informed approach, but there's still a lot of work to do. “The pursuit of medals over human rights or over safety is completely unacceptable, but we know it still happens.” Reuters
item.content:encoded: The judge who sentenced USA Gymnastics doctor Larry Nassar to up to 175 years in prison for sexual abuse has said the sport is still failing athletes in “almost every way” a decade on from the case. Judge Rosemarie Aquilina said reforms introduced since his prolific offending against more than 250 women and girls was exposed largely amounted to “window dressing” and said athletes remained afraid to speak out because of the possible consequences. She told Reuters : “I think that what they've done across the world is window dressing to say, ‘Look at us, look what we've done so well’, and they're still not being accountable for the things that they're not doing. “Safety is a human right and yet these athletes still feel that they don't have it because the sport they love will go away if they complain about anything and so we haven't come far ⁠enough at all. “I don't think we're going to see a change in my lifetime. I think it's going to take decades.” World Gymnastics and USA Gymnastics were not immediately available to comment. Aquilina was speaking at an event organised by Gymnasts for Change International in Rotterdam, where the World Championships are being held this week, to assess progress made on athlete welfare since Nassar was sentenced in 2018. Kim Shore of Gymnasts for Change Canada credited the sport’s governing body World Gymnastics for the positive progress made, but highlighted the wide variation in the sport around the world and the challenge of implementing reforms and safeguards at every level, including grassroots gymnastics. She said: “What we still consistently hear is that there's very much a control dominance style of coaching that is pervasive in the sport, which means that gymnasts don't have a strong voice. “There's still yelling, training on injuries, body shaming, preoccupation with thinness.” Shore said one encouraging shift was that athletes were increasingly staying in the sport beyond their teenage years, with gymnasts competing into their late 20s and some returning after having children. The discussion took place as World Gymnastics prepares to appoint ‌a new secretary general in the coming months, with Swiss Nicolas Buompane stepping down at the end of 2026. Minky Worden of Human Rights Watch said progress had been made in the processes for athletes to report abuse but said the new leadership should prioritise gymnasts’ health and welfare over silverware. She said: “Now I think there are better, not perfect, reporting systems in place... I think there are whistleblower protections, and there is a more trauma-informed approach, but there's still a lot of work to do. “The pursuit of medals over human rights or over safety is completely unacceptable, but we know it still happens.” Reuters

Arsenal , Liverpool , Real Madrid and Aston Villa have also started the Champions League with consecutive wins and Unai Emery’s side enter the top 10 of our rankings at the expense of Manchester United , whose difficult season continued with defeat at Atletico Madrid. We compiled our 36-team power rankings by combining team’s previous performance in the Champions League, their results in the competition so far, and the likelihood of them going all the way this season. It reinforces the idea that Luis Enrique’s team know how to peak at the right time, as they have proved in becoming back-to-back defending champions. PSG are still the team to beat, and will be even if they slip outside of the top eight of the league phase for the third season in a row. Could we see another statement at home to Barcelona? item.content:encoded: Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona head into tonight’s Champions League clash on the back of statement away performances and back-to-back victories. Holders PSG produced a first-half masterclass before holding on top beat Manchester City 4-2 at the Etihad while Barcelona were among the goals once again as Lamine Yamal starred in a 4-1 comeback win at Galatasaray. Arsenal , Liverpool , Real Madrid and Aston Villa have also started the Champions League with consecutive wins and Unai Emery’s side enter the top 10 of our rankings at the expense of Manchester United , whose difficult season continued with defeat at Atletico Madrid. We compiled our 36-team power rankings by combining team’s previous performance in the Champions League, their results in the competition so far, and the likelihood of them going all the way this season. Agree or disagree with our standings? Let us know and have your say in the comments below. ↔️ 1. Paris Saint-Germain Results: 6-1 vs Slovan Bratislava, 4-2 v Man City Fixtures: Barcelona (h), Villarreal (a), Roma (h), Aston Villa (a), Como (a), Galatasaray (h) There were two sides to PSG’s display in the six-goal thriller against Manchester City but holy moly was that first half one of the most impressive performances the Champions League has seen in recent years. It reinforces the idea that Luis Enrique’s team know how to peak at the right time, as they have proved in becoming back-to-back defending champions. PSG are still the team to beat, and will be even if they slip outside of the top eight of the league phase for the third season in a row. Could we see another statement at home to Barcelona? Dembele and Doue both scored as PSG hit three goals in the first half at Manchester City (Getty) ⬆️ 🟢 2. Barcelona (+1 from 3) Results: 5-1 v Feyenoord, 4-1 v Galatasaray Fixtures: PSG (a), Aston Villa (h), Sabah (a), Manchester City (h), Sporting (a), Como (h) Yep, Barcelona still cannot stop scoring, with their comeback victory over Galatasaray taking Hansi Flick’s side to an astonishing 48 goals in their first 11 games of the season. Lamine Yamal’s outrageous turn and close control for his assist for Anthony Gordon was the pick of the goals from Istanbul and there is little doubt that Barcelona are Europe’s in-form side after 11 consecutive wins in all competitions. Whether the defence holds up come the knockout stages is another question, but for now Barcelona’s attack is unstoppable, inspiring confidence that they could compete for a first Champions League crown since 2015. The trip to holders Paris Saint-Germain already looks like a mouthwatering clash. ⬇️ 🔴 3. Arsenal (-1 from 2) Results: 1-0 vs Napoli, 3-0 v Lille Fixtures: Bayern Munich (a), Slavia Prague (a), Borussia Dortmund (h), Real Madrid (h), Real Betis (a), Sabah (h) With two wins from two it has been a typically assured start from last season’s runners-up, who are determined to go one better after their heartbreaking defeat on penalties to PSG. It remains to be seen if Mikel Arteta’s side can take the next step against a heavyweight side in the business end of the Champions League, but their unrivalled squad depth means the Gunners have a very good chance of finishing one of the top two spots in this season’s group phase. Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard were summoned off the bench to spark Arsenal into life for the 3-0 win over Lille; flashes of style from the Gunners are to be welcomed, but are they still missing the firepower of a PSG or Barcelona? Bukayo Saka wrapped up the victory for Arsenal (Reuters) ⬆️ 🟢 4. Man City (+1 from 5) Results: 2-0 v Porto, 2-4 v PSG Fixtures: AEK Athens (h), Leipzig (a), Napoli (h), Barcelona (a), Lens (a), Sporting (a) No one knows what Manchester City’s season from here is going to look like. Could the Champions League become their top target if they are ruled out of the Premier League title race, for instance? No one knows. Still, there is quality and spirit throughout the team – as shown in a strong start domestically and in the second half of their 4-2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain where Enzo Maresca’s side actually come pretty close to mounting an unbelievable fightback . (AP) ⬇️ 🔴 5. Bayern Munich (-1 from 4) Results: 5-0 v Bodo/Glimt, 3-3 v Viking Fixtures: Arsenal (h), Atletico Madrid (a), Lille (a), Slavia Prague (h), Manchester United (a), Real Betis (h) The German champions were stung by Viking in a 3-3 thriller, in the second part of their double-header against teams from Norway following their opening win over Bodo/Glimt. Harry Kane surpassed Lionel Messi’s record for most Champions League goals after turning 30 with a brace, although a silly red card for Michael Olise means he will now be suspended for this week’s home clash against Arsenal. Certainly, if Kane continues his astonishing rate of goalscoring then Bayern will be there or thereabouts. Kane has now scored in nine consecutive Champions League games for Bayern (Reuters) ↔️ 6. Real Madrid Results: 2-1 v Inter Milan, 4-3 v Roma Fixtures: RB Leipzig (h), AEK Athens (a), PSV (h), Arsenal (a), LASK (h), Shakhtar (a) Real Madrid were second best in both of their first two games in the Champions League and yet have six points under Jose Mourinho after beating Inter Milan and Roma. Performances are unconvincing, to say the least, but the 15-time Champions League winners still carry an aura in this competition and have so far offered a bit of a throwback to the days of Carlo Ancelotti. Inter were in control at the Bernabeu but found themselves trailing 2-0 as Real Madrid inevitably scored from their first two shots. Then Roma led 3-1 at the Stadio Olimpico, only to concede three goals from set-pieces as Real Madrid came from behind to win. Real Madrid got out of jail as Rudiger scored a late winner against Roma (Getty) ↔️ 7. Liverpool Results: 2-1 v Atletico Madrid, 6-3 v LASK Fixtures: Villarreal (h), Fenerbahce (a), Club Brugge (a), Porto (h), Inter (a), Lens (h) Still sitting outside the top tier of contenders, you’d have to say it would be a surprise for Liverpool (or any of the teams below the Reds in these rankings) to win the Champions League in their first season under Andoni Iraola. But Bradley Barcola’s hat-trick and an improved attacking display in the 6-3 win at LASK showed the potential of Iraola’s side if he can also get a tune out of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, and Hugo Ekitike when he comes back from injury. A relatively kind fixture list helps, as does Liverpool’s record in the Champions League in recent years. It has taken PSG to knock them out in the last two seasons. Bradley Barcola scored a hat-trick as Liverpool thrashed LASK 6-3 (PA Wire) ⬆️ 🟢 8. Atletico Madrid (+1 from 9) Results: 1-2 v Liverpool, 2-0 v Manchester United Fixtures: Stuttgart (a), Bayern Munich (h), Viking (h), PSV (a), Bodo/Glimt (a), Fenerbahce (h) Last season’s semi-finalists have the added motivation of hosting this season’s Champions League final at the Metropolitano in Madrid and Diego Simeone’s side have clicked into form with five consecutive victories in all competitions since defeat at Anfield. While it would be another colossal overachievement from Simeone to get Atleti into a third Champions League final of his 16-year reign, his side were impressive in beating Manchester United. You know what you’re going to get from a Simeone side in the Champions League but Alex Baena and Pablo Barrios have also added a touch of class into midfield, too. Atletico defeated Barcelona in last season’s quarter-finals and can embrace the underdog role (Getty) ⬇️ 🔴 9. item.title: Mourinho has no plans to change 28-year-old Real Madrid star’s secondary role – report
item.description: Mourinho has no plans to change 28-year-old Real Madrid star’s secondary role – report Jose Mourinho remains unconvinced by Trent Alexander-Arnold at Real Madrid, with the England international struggling to establish himself as a regular starter and facing growing competition for a place in the team. Despite entering his second season at the Santiago Bernabeu, Alexander-Arnold has yet to deliver the consistency required to secure the right-back position. Hence, Mourinho continues to favour other options, leaving the former Liverpool defender with an uncertain role under the Portuguese coach. Why Alexander-Arnold has fallen behind Alexander-Arnold, 28, arrived with a reputation built on his exceptional distribution, crossing and ability to create chances from deep. Those qualities can make him a valuable attacking weapon, but his defensive limitations have repeatedly complicated his bid to become an automatic starter. However, as reported by Defensa Central , Mourinho has yet to see enough to change that assessment. The Portuguese coach requested Dumfries when he arrived at the club, valuing the Dutchman’s defensive capabilities alongside his ability to contribute in attack. Trent Alexander-Arnold is losing Mourinho’s confidence. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) That preference is particularly revealing because Dumfries has struggled to reproduce his Inter Milan form. Yet Alexander-Arnold has still been unable to take advantage. Dumfries and Valverde give Mourinho alternatives Mourinho initially explored a way to use both full-backs together during pre-season, potentially combining Dumfries’ defensive strength with Alexander-Arnold’s creativity. However, the emergence of Diomande and Arda Guler’s involvement in wide areas have complicated the prospect of finding a consistent role for the Englishman. Valverde creates another problem for Alexander-Arnold because his versatility gives Mourinho an additional option on the right. Rather than building the position around one specialist, the manager can choose between different profiles depending on the team’s needs. As far as Dumfries is concerned, he has played 568 minutes under Mourinho, but in the last few matches, even he has appeared to have lost the manager’s confidence. Can Alexander-Arnold offer Mourinho a solution elsewhere? The Champions League fixture against Inter provided another test of Alexander-Arnold’s adaptability. What happens next with Trent Alexander-Arnold? (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) With several players unavailable, Mourinho tried him in central midfield, a position he had previously occupied for England. The experiment did not yield the desired result, exposing concerns about his ability to control matches under pressure and withstand physical challenges. That failed switch matters because versatility could have offered Alexander-Arnold another route into the starting team. Instead, his midfield display did little to resolve the question of where he fits best.

However, as reported by Defensa Central , Mourinho has yet to see enough to change that assessment. The Portuguese coach requested Dumfries when he arrived at the club, valuing the Dutchman’s defensive capabilities alongside his ability to contribute in attack. Trent Alexander-Arnold is losing Mourinho’s confidence. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) That preference is particularly revealing because Dumfries has struggled to reproduce his Inter Milan form. Yet Alexander-Arnold has still been unable to take advantage. Dumfries and Valverde give Mourinho alternatives Mourinho initially explored a way to use both full-backs together during pre-season, potentially combining Dumfries’ defensive strength with Alexander-Arnold’s creativity. However, the emergence of Diomande and Arda Guler’s involvement in wide areas have complicated the prospect of finding a consistent role for the Englishman. Valverde creates another problem for Alexander-Arnold because his versatility gives Mourinho an additional option on the right. Rather than building the position around one specialist, the manager can choose between different profiles depending on the team’s needs. As far as Dumfries is concerned, he has played 568 minutes under Mourinho, but in the last few matches, even he has appeared to have lost the manager’s confidence. Can Alexander-Arnold offer Mourinho a solution elsewhere? The Champions League fixture against Inter provided another test of Alexander-Arnold’s adaptability. What happens next with Trent Alexander-Arnold? (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) With several players unavailable, Mourinho tried him in central midfield, a position he had previously occupied for England. The experiment did not yield the desired result, exposing concerns about his ability to control matches under pressure and withstand physical challenges. That failed switch matters because versatility could have offered Alexander-Arnold another route into the starting team. Instead, his midfield display did little to resolve the question of where he fits best. His clearest route back may therefore be at right-back , where his passing and crossing remain valuable assets. But to change Mourinho’s view, Alexander-Arnold must show that those attacking qualities can be delivered without leaving the team exposed defensively. Until then, his place at Real Madrid will remain a contest rather than a guarantee.

item.title: ‘Insane,’ ‘Caitlin Clark Won’t Break This Record’ — WNBA Fans Hail Angel Reese As Dream Star Makes History in Atlanta’s 1st-Ever Finals Win
item.description: 'Insane,' 'Caitlin Clark Won't Break This Record' -- WNBA Fans Hail Angel Reese As Dream Star Makes History in Atlanta's 1st-Ever Finals Win The Atlanta Dream’s 79-65 win over the Golden State Valkyries in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals had Angel Reese’s imprint all over it. The three-time WNBA All-Star erupted for a 30-point, 16-rebound double-double, dismantling a Valkyries defense that had been one of the league’s best all postseason, and fans couldn’t help but marvel at Reese’s historic night. WNBA Fans Buzzing Over Angel Reese’s Historic Double-Double in Dream’s Game 2 Finals Win Reese and the Dream were coming off a frustrating Game 1 defeat where the Valkyries managed to completely shut down the star forward in the second half. The 24-year-old came out firing on all cylinders in Game 2, never allowing the Valkyries to slow her down this time. At the final buzzer, Reese’s stat line read: 30 points, 16 rebounds, 3 assists, 1 steal, 2 blocks on 10-of-16 shooting from the field and 9-of-11 from the charity stripe. SportsCenter captured the scale of her performance , posting, “ANGEL REESE HISTORIC GAME 2 👑 She’s just the third player in WNBA history with 30 points and 15 rebounds in a Finals game.” ESPN Insights added another context to Reese’s achievement, writing , “OH WHAT A NIGHT 🏀 Angel Reese is also the first player in Dream history with 25 PTS and 10 REB in a playoff game!” Underdog WNBA went further, putting her performance in historical context: “Youngest player with a 20-point double-double, WNBA Finals history: Angel Reese – 24 years, 166 days (tonight). Cappie Pondexter – 24 years, 252 days (2007). Jonquel Jones – 25 years, 269 days (2019).” Reese’s historic production helped Atlanta even the best-of-seven series at 1-1. Fans have nothing but praise for the Dream star. “Insane,” one fan simply put it . Another fan took a shot at comparisons to the league’s other biggest star, writing , “Caitlin Clark won’t break this record btw.” The numbers alone would have been enough to generate buzz, but the moment carried extra weight given where Reese was just six months earlier. She was traded from the Chicago Sky to Atlanta in April 2026, a move that followed a turbulent second season in Chicago, which included a half-game suspension for comments she made about the team’s direction. item.title: Terry McLaurin Injury Could be ‘Significant,’ Says Dan Quinn
item.description: Terry McLaurin Commanders Dan Quinn Getty Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said that wide receiver Terry McLaurin’s injury could be “significant.” McLaurin left the Commanders’ 23-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in the first quarter with an apparent knee injury, one that Quinn says has the team in “fear” for the worst possible outcome. Dan Quinn Worried About Terry McLaurin’s Injury Speaking to the media following the Commanders’ loss to the 49ers, Quinn admitted that there is “fear” amongst the team’s staff that McLaurin may have suffered a “significant” injury. “The concern is that it could be significant, but we’ll do the scans tomorrow and give you an update. But it’s definitely something that there’s fear,” Quinn said. As Quinn noted, the media will be provided an update on Tuesday once McLaurin’s medical scans are completed. But clearly, based on the way he spoke to the media tonight after the Commanders’ loss to the 49ers, Quinn is very worried that he might lose his Pro Bowl wide receiver. Commanders Need Terry McLaurin With McLaurin potentially being seriously injured, the Commanders could be in big trouble going forward, as he is the team’s best wide receiver and the top weapon for QB Jayden Daniels . McLaurin has already missed time this year with a hamstring injury, so to see him potentially seriously injured here is yet another tough blow for a Commanders squad that really cannot afford to lose any more games. Following their loss to San Francisco, the 49ers are just 1-4-1 on the season and in last place in the NFC East. However, the good news for the Commanders is that the rest of their division isn’t exactly lighting the world on fire, so believe it or not, Washington still has a chance to make the playoffs if they can string some wins together. But losing McLaurin hurts, as the two-time Pro Bowler has been one of the best wide receivers in the NFL ever since he entered the league in 2019. He has been banged up the past two seasons, playing in just 10 games last year and then parts of five this season while dealing with injuries, which clearly hurts the Commanders, who rely on him for explosive plays and scoring touchdowns. If McLaurin is going to be out for a while, then the Commanders may have to go out and make a trade to bring in some help at the WR spot for the rest of the season. The team still has a chance to make a playoff run if they can string a few wins together, but Daniels needs some help, as he can’t do everything on his own. If McLaurin is indeed going to be out for some time, then the team can only hope that someone else steps up in his absence and that the rest of the players can rally around their fallen teammate and make a big run after their bye week next week as the Commanders look to turn their season around and help Quinn save his coaching job. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Terry McLaurin Injury Could be ‘Significant,’ Says Dan Quinn appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Fantasy Football Running Back Rankings: Week 7 2026
item.description: Fantasy Football Running Back Rankings: Week 7 2026 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Fantasy football managers entering Week 7 have plenty to consider when setting their running back lineups, from dominant workhorses to emerging alternatives benefiting from injuries. With several notable running backs dealing with injuries or uncertain availability, monitoring workload trends, and late-week updates will be essential. Here are the top picks and sleepers to consider for Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season. Week 7 Top Fantasy Football Picks Jahmyr Gibbs , DET (vs. GB) Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Jahmyr Gibbs remains one of fantasy football’s most valuable running backs . That’s after another dominant performance in Week 6. Gibbs rushed 25 times for 151 yards and two touchdowns while catching five passes for 56 yards, surpassing 200 total yards, and finding the end zone twice. That combination of rushing volume, receiving involvement, and touchdown production makes Gibbs an elite fantasy asset. A Week 7 matchup against Green Bay presents another opportunity for Gibbs to deliver. As long as he remains healthy and maintains his current role, Gibbs belongs among the very top running backs in fantasy football. Gibbs is the clear headliner this week. He should be locked into every lineup where he is available. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Bijan Robinson , ATL (vs. SF) Bijan Robinson had an unusually quiet outing in Atlanta’s 31-23 Week 6 loss to Chicago . He rushed nine times for 61 yards while catching both of his targets for minus-eight receiving yards. His total offensive production fell below 70 yards for the first time in six contests. Sure, the performance was disappointing. However, it should not trigger a major reassessment of Robinson’s fantasy football value. Robinson faces the San Francisco 49ers in Week 7. This matchup will be challenging. Still, his workload and talent keep him firmly in RB1 territory. Fantasy managers should resist the temptation to bench him after one disappointing performance. Robinson remains a must-start RB1 in all formats. Trust his established role rather than overreacting to one quiet week. Kenneth Walker III , KC (@ SEA) Kenneth Walker III delivered one of Week 6’s most impressive running back performances. He rushed 19 times for 128 yards and two touchdowns. He also caught two of three targets for 11 yards. That gives him additional value beyond his rushing production. His numbers demonstrate the combination of efficiency and workload that fantasy football managers want from a top-tier running back. His recent performance gives managers little reason to hesitate. Walker is generating productive runs while receiving enough opportunities to remain a reliable fantasy starter. If that workload continues, he should have another chance to deliver RB1 numbers in Week 7 against Seattle. Walker is a high-end RB1 after his explosive Week 6 outing. Week 7 Fantasy

item.title: ‘Say Your Apology on Air’ — Eagles Legend Terrell Owens Calls Out Michael Robinson’s Response to Jalen Hurts Controversy
item.description: ‘Say Your Apology on Air’ — Eagles Legend Terrell Owens Calls Out Michael Robinson’s Response to Jalen Hurts Controversy Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 NFL season after being diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in his left calf and blood clots in both lungs. After the diagnosis was announced, NFL Network analyst Michael Robinson apologized for questioning Hurts’ commitment to the team last week. However, former Eagles star Terrell Owens was not satisfied with Robinson’s written apology and called on him to address his comments on television. Terrell Owens Criticizes Robinson’s Apology Over Jalen Hurts Comments Owens did not hold back when reacting to Robinson’s apology on Instagram. “Say your apology on air as you did the disrespect,” Owens wrote. “This is where getting too cute with the commentary goes wrong!” The controversy began after Hurts was diagnosed with a superficial blood clot during an ultrasound in London on Oct. 10. He played against the Jacksonville Jaguars without limitations Sunday, Oct. 11, but further tests the following Wednesday revealed that the clot had shifted. As a result, the star quarterback missed Philadelphia’s Week 6 matchup against the Carolina Panthers, which the Eagles lost 25-14. On Monday, the Eagles and Hurts’ agent confirmed that further testing had revealed deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport and ESPN’s Adam Schefter subsequently reported that Hurts is expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Before the full diagnosis became public, Robinson questioned whether the quarterback was using his injury as a reason to sit out, given the state of the team. “This is just me outside looking in. I don’t know nothing, guys. But it looked like they were trying to pin the outcome of this season on Jalen Hurts, just so that they can have an excuse later on to move on from Jalen Hurts,” Robinson began on “NFL GameDay Kickoff.” “But if I’m just playing devil’s advocate here, and I’m thinking that way, if I’m Jalen Hurts… or anybody in Jalen Hurts’ camp… I’m saying, ‘Well, if everybody’s hurt, I’m hurt, too.’ To me, it looked like Jalen is kind of getting himself out of the fray… he’s pulling himself out so that this [lost season] doesn’t look like it’s on him.” SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer Following the Eagles’ announcement about Hurts’ diagnosis, Robinson apologized to the quarterback, his family, the organization, and its fans. “I want to sincerely apologize to Jalen Hurts, his family, the Philadelphia Eagles organization and fanbase for my comments last Thursday. They were unfounded, and I never should’ve speculated on a health issue of a player, nor his commitment to his team,” Robinson wrote. Although Robinson acknowledged that his comments were wrong, Owens believes he should make the same apology “on air,” given that his original comments were made on television. PREDICT THE NFL

item.title: Whither Vladimir? (Part 1)
item.description: TORONTO, ON - SEPTEMBER 27: Toronto Blue Jays infielder Vladimir Guerrero Jr. (27) is seen in the Blue Jays dugout during the first inning of an MLB game between the Cincinnati Reds and the Toronto Blue Jays on September 27, 2026, at Rogers Centre in Toronto, ON. (Photo by Mathew Tsang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It’s no secret that a big part of the Blue Jays’ disappointing 2026 was the result of a disastrous season by superstar first baseman Vladimir Guerrero jr. Vlad’s offensive production cratered, from an average wRC+ of 139 from 2023-2025 to 95 this past season. If the team’s going to get back into contention in 2027 and beyond, it’s going to have to start with a bounce back from Guerrero. I wanted to try to figure out what went wrong and how likely it is to be fixed for next year. Today, I’m going to look for some historically comparable collapses and see what we can learn from them. Later this week I’ll dive deeper into the stats to try to figure out what exactly went wrong. Usually when a player’s performance falls off dramatically, the culprit is either age or injury. Neither really fits here, though. Vlad was definitely banged up this season, missing time with finger, elbow, back, and hamstring injuries plus a concussion. He also got laser eye surgery after the season. Still, he played 144 games and took 609 PA, and no one of the injuries really coincides with a huge drop off in production. Plus, he put up the best base running and defensive metrics of his career. He was clearly moving well everywhere but in the batter’s box. The nicks and dents could explain some struggles, but nothing of this magnitude. As for age, at 27 he should just be reaching his peak, not falling from it. To find comparable stretches, I looked for period of four consecutive seasons where a batter qualified for the batting title each time (so presumably excluding catastrophic injuries) and was 30 or younger in the final season (mostly avoiding age related decline). In the integration era, there have been 1,852 such runs (excluding ones that end in a season shortened due to strike or plague). item.content:encoded: TORONTO, ON - SEPTEMBER 27: Toronto Blue Jays infielder Vladimir Guerrero Jr. (27) is seen in the Blue Jays dugout during the first inning of an MLB game between the Cincinnati Reds and the Toronto Blue Jays on September 27, 2026, at Rogers Centre in Toronto, ON. (Photo by Mathew Tsang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It’s no secret that a big part of the Blue Jays’ disappointing 2026 was the result of a disastrous season by superstar first baseman Vladimir Guerrero jr. Vlad’s offensive production cratered, from an average wRC+ of 139 from 2023-2025 to 95 this past season. If the team’s going to get back into contention in 2027 and beyond, it’s going to have to start with a bounce back from Guerrero. I wanted to try to figure out what went wrong and how likely it is to be fixed for next year. Today, I’m going to look for some historically comparable collapses and see what we can learn from them. Later this week I’ll dive deeper into the stats to try to figure out what exactly went wrong. Usually when a player’s performance falls off dramatically, the culprit is either age or injury. Neither really fits here, though. Vlad was definitely banged up this season, missing time with finger, elbow, back, and hamstring injuries plus a concussion. He also got laser eye surgery after the season. Still, he played 144 games and took 609 PA, and no one of the injuries really coincides with a huge drop off in production. Plus, he put up the best base running and defensive metrics of his career. He was clearly moving well everywhere but in the batter’s box. The nicks and dents could explain some struggles, but nothing of this magnitude. As for age, at 27 he should just be reaching his peak, not falling from it. To find comparable stretches, I looked for period of four consecutive seasons where a batter qualified for the batting title each time (so presumably excluding catastrophic injuries) and was 30 or younger in the final season (mostly avoiding age related decline). In the integration era, there have been 1,852 such runs (excluding ones that end in a season shortened due to strike or plague). As the graph below shows, most players perform about the same in year 4 compared to the average of years 1-3. Only 11 players had declines in wRC+ as extreme as Vlad’s -45 points. Already we can see that we’re in strange waters. I found 18 other players who experienced a drop of 40-50 points of wRC+, within 5 points of Vlad’s. Here’s what those seasons looked like: The median is in blue, Vlad is in orange. You can see that he’s been a more volatile player than his comps even before this season, posting both the best and the worst seasons relative to average in the baseline three year period. The overall pattern is similar, though: players were mostly bouncing around in a range of plus or minus 20 points before falling off a cliff in year four. So what happened to these guys? The next graph breaks the fall down into the impacts of power (measured as change in ISO), strikeouts, walks, batting average on balls in play (BABIP) and variance not explained by those other factors. It’s based on a regression model predicting changes in wRC+ based on the four stats mentioned before. Most players got worse across the board. To fall off this badly you can’t just have one thing go wrong. Still, there are definite groups. Vlad’s performance was driven mostly by a power outage, while his BABIP and walks fell only slightly and he actually cut his strikeout rate a little. BABIP and ‘other’ are the things that have to the most to do with luck or outside circumstances, and they don’t seem to have been a huge factor here. That puts him closer to the likes of Travis Hafner and Albert Belle and farther from Dave May or Delino DeShields. In fact, the decline in ISO accounts for 69% of his wRC+ decline, the largest among the comps. So this kind of decline has happened before, and to some excellent players, but it’s still rare. What can history tell us about Vlad’s likely perfromance going forward? The graph below extends the previous wRC+ chart through years 5-9. It’s not enormously comforting. the group did bounce back, on average, but not to pre-dip norms. The median player recovered about 10-15 points of their initial 45 point drop for the next three seasons before beginning to decline due to age. For Jays fans, that’s a scary set of comps. It suggests that Vlad should be able to get back to being a decent hitter, but maybe only a decent one rather than the superstar that his $500 million contract demands. There are some reasons for a little more optimism, though. The players in the sample who were 28 or younger in year 4 were about twice as likely to bounce back to within 10 points of wRC+ of their previous performance than those who were 29 or 30. Vlad is among the youngest players in the group. Those whose fall off was driven more then 50% by a power outage had a better than 50% chance of getting back, while those whose dip was driven by strikeouts, walks or BABIP had a less than 20% chance. Finally, some of the players who never returned to their previous level showed other signs of physical decline. Andre Dawson, for example, saw his steal attempts cut in half while moving from centre field to right, suggesting that while he didn’t actually miss time the knee troubles that would dog the back half of his career were already hurting him. There are a few other non-recoverers with similar clear signs of decline. As mentioned above, Vlad’s athleticism (never the core of his game) looked as good as it ever has. The injuries that bothered him this year were mostly from hit by pitches and other freak events, and there’s no reason to worry that his body is giving out. There appears to be a real risk that Vlad won’t be the same player he used to be, based on the history of players with similar issues, but the demographic factors look like they’re all in his favour.

item.title: Shrewsbury takeover in 'final stages' - Wycherley
item.description: Shrewsbury Town owner Roland Wycherley first began looking to attract new investors at the Shropshire club in 2021 [Nathan Stirk - Getty Images] Shrewsbury Town owner Roland Wycherley has responded to another open letter from impatient Salop fans by saying "public pressure" is not a "constructive approach" to his process of concluding the sale of the League Two club. Ten Town supporters' groups came together on Monday to ask for "clarity" over the timescale of the Shropshire club's proposed takeover by an American consortium, led by Miami-based Scott Davidson and two of his fellow directors at Scottish League Two club, The Spartans - Will Dotson and Craig Graham - plus former USA goalkeeper Brad Friedel. Despite Wycherley's previous plea for patience, Town fans have become frustrated over growing speculation, reported on BBC Radio Shropshire, that Wycherley might not now want to sell - and that the club might even instead be working on an alternative deal. But a statement released in response by the club insists "the process is continuing to move forward and is now in its final stages". The club are particularly upset at the timing of the latest fans' letter, in the wake of an improved run of 11 points out of a possible 18 from their past six games to help Salop climb to 14th in the table - and little more than 24 hours before a key trip to bottom club Crawley Town. The united Town fans, bracketed under the label of 'Floreat Salopia' - in homage to the Latin motto on both the Shropshire county crest and on the club badge - later responded to the club's statement by saying that "an absence of information can lead to dangerous speculation". Meanwhile, in Monday evening's televised draw , Shrewsbury were handed a long away trip in the FA Cup first round on the weekend of 6-9 November - having been paired with Hampshire side Eastleigh, who sit 17th in the National League. Prospective Salop owners get dual interest clearance Wycherley asks for fans' patience over Shrewsbury takeover Davidson's US Shrewsbury takeover involves Friedel The Shrewsbury Town board's response "Shrewsbury Town is aware of a letter published requesting public comment on the ongoing takeover of the club. "The letter states that "we have had no indication of progress" on the proposed takeover since Scott Davidson received approval from the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) to acquire the club. We do not agree with this assessment. "On September 18, the club published a statement confirming that Craig Graham and Will Dotson had successfully completed the relevant owners' and directors' tests. "A further statement on September 25 confirmed Brad Friedel had also received IFR approval. "We believe this demonstrates the club has provided updates where publicly appropriate. "We remain committed to progressing all matters relating to the proposed takeover through the appropriate channels as soon as possible. The united Town fans, bracketed under the label of 'Floreat Salopia' - in homage to the Latin motto on both the Shropshire county crest and on the club badge - later responded to the club's statement by saying that "an absence of information can lead to dangerous speculation". Prospective Salop owners get dual interest clearance Wycherley asks for fans' patience over Shrewsbury takeover Davidson's US Shrewsbury takeover involves Friedel The Shrewsbury Town board's response "Shrewsbury Town is aware of a letter published requesting public comment on the ongoing takeover of the club. "The letter states that "we have had no indication of progress" on the proposed takeover since Scott Davidson received approval from the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) to acquire the club. We do not agree with this assessment. "On September 18, the club published a statement confirming that Craig Graham and Will Dotson had successfully completed the relevant owners' and directors' tests. "A further statement on September 25 confirmed Brad Friedel had also received IFR approval. "We believe this demonstrates the club has provided updates where publicly appropriate. "We remain committed to progressing all matters relating to the proposed takeover through the appropriate channels as soon as possible. "We do not believe that applying public pressure, demanding comments to rumours, or issuing threats is a constructive approach while the takeover process continues to move forward. "The club remains committed to handling all takeover-related matters professionally, respectfully and through the proper channels. We will not be drawn into repeated public exchanges and ask that this position is respected. "We would like to thank all supporters who continue to back the club and recognise that not every matter can, or should, be addressed publicly."

item.title: The Steph Curry scare that reveals the NBA’s hidden problem
item.description: Steph Curry flapped his arms and ripped the gumshield from his mouth and stumbled towards the locker room. The open practice for the Warriors, 48 hours before the 2026/27 NBA season gets underway, delivered a chill throughout the arena. A deathly silence was palpable, knowing the precarious foundation of the Golden State’s hopes and dreams, pinned to No 30. LeBron James ’s seismic switch from Los Angeles to Philadelphia has somewhat obscured the curious situation of a 38-year-old legend’s final act. In the immediate aftermath of Curry’s misstep, irresponsible speculation spread of an ACL tear, which would all but scupper an 18th NBA season. But news since has confirmed the issue was merely a right ankle injury, with Curry initially maintaining he was “fine” before Golden State head coach Steve Kerr cleared him for the season opener against the Los Angeles Lakers on Wednesday night. But this injury scare underlined a growing concern for the Warriors. And beyond an inevitable rebuild in a post-Curry world, the NBA’s grand plans for global relevance are up against the might of the NFL’s dominance and ambitious competition from other sports internationally. And in this star-driven league, given the NFL is not necessarily built the same way, the NBA is experiencing a changing of the guard with an influx of international superstars after a soon-to-be nine-year gap since the last American MVP (James Harden in 2017/18). The NBA was absent from the 2025 Sportico 100, which showcases the most-watched US telecasts each year, a sixth straight year, with the American gluttony for the NFL illustrated by 84 events in the list. For those already initiated, the NBA is a compelling product and at first glance should soar in the coming years. Just look at last year’s finals and the Knicks’ first title in 53 years. The captivating nature of Jalen Brunson guiding New York past the Spurs, led by the most talented player of a generation, Victor Wembanyama, who emerged as a villain in the Big Apple, sets the table for a generation-defining rivalry. The precarious foundation of the Golden State’s hopes and dreams are pinned to No 30, Curry (AP) This writer witnessed how World Cup mania belatedly arrived in New York thanks to that Knicks run , underlining that the ingredients are there to muscle in on the NFL and Premier League in the relentless pursuit for content. There have been eight different champions in as many years, though the league must better harness that unpredictable nature to thrive. A ninth could emerge in Philadelphia, with LeBron James, seeking title No 5 and aiming to snap a seven-year drought, fresh from an unlikely switch from Los Angeles Lakers to 76ers. He joins Jaylen Brown, the Robin to Jayson Tatum as Batman for so long in Boston, alongside Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey to form the latest NBA super team. item.content:encoded: Steph Curry flapped his arms and ripped the gumshield from his mouth and stumbled towards the locker room. The open practice for the Warriors, 48 hours before the 2026/27 NBA season gets underway, delivered a chill throughout the arena. A deathly silence was palpable, knowing the precarious foundation of the Golden State’s hopes and dreams, pinned to No 30. LeBron James ’s seismic switch from Los Angeles to Philadelphia has somewhat obscured the curious situation of a 38-year-old legend’s final act. In the immediate aftermath of Curry’s misstep, irresponsible speculation spread of an ACL tear, which would all but scupper an 18th NBA season. But news since has confirmed the issue was merely a right ankle injury, with Curry initially maintaining he was “fine” before Golden State head coach Steve Kerr cleared him for the season opener against the Los Angeles Lakers on Wednesday night. But this injury scare underlined a growing concern for the Warriors. And beyond an inevitable rebuild in a post-Curry world, the NBA’s grand plans for global relevance are up against the might of the NFL’s dominance and ambitious competition from other sports internationally. And in this star-driven league, given the NFL is not necessarily built the same way, the NBA is experiencing a changing of the guard with an influx of international superstars after a soon-to-be nine-year gap since the last American MVP (James Harden in 2017/18). The NBA was absent from the 2025 Sportico 100, which showcases the most-watched US telecasts each year, a sixth straight year, with the American gluttony for the NFL illustrated by 84 events in the list. For those already initiated, the NBA is a compelling product and at first glance should soar in the coming years. Just look at last year’s finals and the Knicks’ first title in 53 years. The captivating nature of Jalen Brunson guiding New York past the Spurs, led by the most talented player of a generation, Victor Wembanyama, who emerged as a villain in the Big Apple, sets the table for a generation-defining rivalry. The precarious foundation of the Golden State’s hopes and dreams are pinned to No 30, Curry (AP) This writer witnessed how World Cup mania belatedly arrived in New York thanks to that Knicks run , underlining that the ingredients are there to muscle in on the NFL and Premier League in the relentless pursuit for content. There have been eight different champions in as many years, though the league must better harness that unpredictable nature to thrive. A ninth could emerge in Philadelphia, with LeBron James, seeking title No 5 and aiming to snap a seven-year drought, fresh from an unlikely switch from Los Angeles Lakers to 76ers. He joins Jaylen Brown, the Robin to Jayson Tatum as Batman for so long in Boston, alongside Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey to form the latest NBA super team. While two-time reigning MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and the uber efficient Oklahoma City Thunder, champions in 2025, are the favourites once again. Commissioner Adam Silver has genuine authority and ideas, with the NBA Cup adding a wrinkle to major league tradition in the United States. But even with the exciting plans to launch NBA Europe and tie franchises to the continent’s leading football clubs, something is missing. LeBron James, Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey of the Philadelphia 76ers look on (Getty) Speaking about his plans to utilise Curry, though Philadelphia’s Nick Nurse may encounter similar issues with James and the injury-prone Embiid, Kerr spoke of the awkward dilemma surrounding Curry’s usage, perhaps highlighting how the next generation of superstar American basketball players are yet to take the throne of Curry, James and more. Curry remains one of the most compelling athletes in sport, with thousands flocking to catch a glimpse of him during his final years playing. You could feel the allure even outside of NBA circles during the 2024 Olympics two years ago, when Curry elevated his game and captivated a global audience en route to gold. I can even recall the swoosh of the net reverberating around the Bercy Arena, Paris as fans held their breath during Curry’s iconic warm-up routine. “We’ll start trying to map out, week by week, what’s what,” Kerr said of Curry’s usage before that injury scare, with the widely-accepted greatest shooter of all time dealing with a nagging right knee injury that cost him 39 games last term. “But to be really frank, every year we run into this [situation] where, if we have a bunch of games stacked together, back-to-backs, we have fans that buy tickets expecting to see Steph – usually Steph, sometimes other players, people expecting to see vets – and then we have a back-to-back, and we don’t play ’em. So, I would just come out and tell the fans out there to be mindful when you’re buying the tickets of the schedule. Take a look. Because we’ve got not just Steph but multiple vets we are going to try and manage, because it’s the only way we can do this.” Golden State are not alone, but with 15 back-to-backs, the value of those Warriors games are drastically reduced both at the game and on televisions around the world, a growing issue as Silver bids to retain audiences in the regular season before the exhilarating playoffs begin on 13 April with the play-in tournament. Steph Curry is a major doubt for the opening game of the season but appears to have avoided a season-ending injury (AP) Until then, the numerous shooting stars in this sport’s galaxy include the NBA Cup, a Christmas Day feast of five back-to-back games, international games aplenty, including Spurs v Pelicans in Manchester, a trade frenzy building to the 11 February deadline and the ever-evolving All-Star game. Sometimes less is more and protecting Curry, James and the league’s best veteran superstars remains paramount to the league’s ultimate success. The 2026/27 NBA season returns to Sky Sports and NOW from 20 October

item.title: Pedri: Lamine Yamal shouldn't be compared to anyone, not even Lionel Messi
item.description: Pedri: Lamine Yamal shouldn't be compared to anyone, not even Lionel Messi Pedri believes Lamine Yamal should not be compared to anyone, insisting that measuring the youngster against Lionel Messi is "complicated" because it means comparing him to "the best player in history". The comparisons between Lamine and Messi have become a recurring theme, as the teenager continues to break records in Barcelona colours. Yamal’s ascent to, arguably, a status as the world’s best player has mirrored Messi’s own rise at the Camp Nou. Barcelona teammate Pedri is the latest high-profile figure to be asked about them. The Spaniard called comparisons with Messi an unfair burden, with the latter regarded by many as the greatest of all time. “For me, Lamine shouldn't be compared to anyone because comparing him to Leo Messi is complicated… …comparing yourself to the best player in history is complicated.” - Pedri "The best player in the world" That does not mean Pedri held back on his praise. At the same time, he labelled Yamal as football’s current number one. Pedri is not alone in pushing back on the Messi comparison. Earlier in the day, Paris Saint-German head coach Luis Enrique rejected it too. Enrique, who coached Messi during his time as Barcelona boss, will come face-to-face with Yamal when PSG take on the Spanish champions in the Champions League this evening. At his pre-match press conference, he talked down the comparisons. “Lamine-Messi comparisons? You can not compare any player with Messi, he's the best ever.” - Luis Enrique Yamal has started the season in exceptional form, with eight goals and six assists in just nine La Liga appearances. In Europe, he’s been similarly devastating. Yamal has recorded a goal and four assists in only 180 minutes of Champions League football. The teenager is a contender for the Ballon d’Or when it is announced this month, and could become the youngest-ever winner of the award, after a runners-up finish in 2025.

item.title: 'He needs time' - Martin Demichelis insists Franco Mastantuono is built for Real Madrid despite Fiorentina loan spell
item.description: Genoa CFC v ACF Fiorentina - Serie A - Getty Images Sport Former mentor backs Argentine prodigy Demichelis is adamant that his former River Plate pupil Mastantuono possesses the personality, physicality and technical ability to thrive with Los Blancos despite his temporary switch to La Viola. The tactician handed the midfielder his senior bow aged 16 in January 2024 before Madrid completed a €45 million transfer in August 2025 . Now 19, the youngster moved to Italy this term in search of regular first-team football. European adaptation requires patient approach European adaptation requires patient approach Having become the youngest player in history to feature in an official match for Argentina's senior national team at 17 , the playmaker made his Santiago Bernabeu debut on August 20, 2025 as a 68th-minute substitute for Brahim Diaz against Osasuna. Although he arrived as the most expensive signing in Argentine football history on a six-year deal running until June 2031, adjusting to European football's elite level demands patience. Highlighting the need for time while recalling the build-up to the teenager's professional breakthrough during a virtual media roundtable on Monday, Demichelis, as quoted by ESPN Argentina , said: "He needs time. You have to look back at how many South American players have joined top European clubs and gone on to succeed. Santiago Solari or Gonzalo Higuain needed time to adapt to one of the biggest institutions in the world, if not the biggest. Especially when you are that young. "Franco didn't make his debut at 16 by magic. There's a wonderful backstory before he did. I spoke with him, with River's directors, and with his parents to see if they were prepared for what was coming, and also to understand his contract situation. Physically, he was among the top three to five players day in and day out, particularly in recovery; on top of that, he had the personality and temperament to rise to the occasion. I believe Xabi Alonso (at Real Madrid) noted his personality when he first met him." Record release clause foresaw greatness After watching the youngster net his maiden senior goal for the Millonario in a 1-0 win over Sarmiento in July 2024, Demichelis even urged club directors to set his release clause higher than the fee agreed for a fellow academy graduate's move to England. Detailing how he pushed the board to demand a record figure while backing the player's current spell in Serie A, Demichelis added: "The board took note of his situation. At that point, we had sold Claudio Echeverri to Manchester City, and they thought about setting his buyout clause at the same value. But I said no - Franco was going to be a player for Real Madrid. From there, the club did fantastic work with his agent; they set a buyout clause that was unheard of for Argentine football, and it ended up being the biggest sale in the country's history. Impressive Florence start builds momentum Impressive Florence start builds momentum That decision to spend the 2026-27 campaign in Florence is already paying dividends, with Mastantuono scoring three goals across his opening seven Serie A outings. Building on that productive start in Italy's top flight will be vital as he prepares to fight for a starting berth back in the Spanish capital next summer. Meanwhile, Demichelis is preparing his RB Leipzig side to face Madrid in the Champions League this week.

item.title: NFL Insider reveals why Bills must live or die by Josh Allen
item.description: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images NFL Insider reveals why Bills must live or die by Josh Allen appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Buffalo Bills have centered their Super Bowl aspirations around quarterback Josh Allen . With a 5-1 record after Week 6 win , Buffalo is making progress toward meeting its high expectations this season. NFL insider Danny Parkins believes the team must continue putting its faith in its franchise quarterback if it hopes to accomplish its ultimate goal of winning a championship. On First Things First, Parkins explained why the Bills must accept both the rewards and risks of building their offense around Allen. “To live by the Josh, die by the Josh,” Parkins said. “That’s how it works. You’re gonna hope that he gets hot for 3 or 4 games in the playoffs and wins you a Super Bowl as the most talented player in football and yeah, you’re gonna live with some interceptions.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Allen has played a crucial role in the Bills’ impressive start to the season. Through six games, he has recorded 1,504 passing yards, nine passing touchdowns and four interceptions while completing 66.7% of his attempts. The Bills quarterback has also contributed 240 rushing yards and eight rushing touchdowns. Allen’s latest outing against the Las Vegas Raiders provided another example of his influence on the team. He completed 23 of 33 passes for 255 yards and two touchdowns, helping Buffalo secure a narrow 33-30 victory. The quarterback’s ability to make exceptional plays and carry the offense gives the Bills a significant advantage, but that same approach can result in interceptions. Hence, Parkins thinks Buffalo must be willing to accept those risks and trust Allen to deliver a series of outstanding performances when the playoffs arrive. Allen and Buffalo will next take on the Baltimore Ravens to continue their championship dream. item.title: Two Celtic Players Ruled Out vs Celta Vigo Already
item.description: With a 7-1 win over Hearts at the weekend, Celtic have every reason to be confident going into their matchup against Celta Vigo this week, even though they have lost both their Europa League matchups so far. That does mean that Celtic are under pressure to get a result against Celta Vigo. If they fail to do so, it would make qualification to the next round of the Europa League very difficult. Unfortunately for Celtic, two of their key players have already been ruled out for their game against Celta Vigo. We have already talked about Yang Hyun-jun not being fit in time to take on Celta Vigo this week. Unfortunately, he is not the only one in that situation. Another Celtic player looks set to miss game against Celta Vigo Cameron Carter-Vickers is another player we have not seen in action over the last few matches for Celtic. Carter-Vickers grabbed the headlines with his comments following Celtic's loss against the Rangers right before the international break. A lot of fans would have been intrigued to see if that would end up having an impact on his place in Martin O'Neill's plans. But due to an injury, he has not even been available since then. As reported by The Celtic Way , O'Neill said when asked whether Carter-Vickers would be available to face Celta Vigo: "Cameron, I think the earliest we'd be probably seeing him would be the Hibs game." So, this is another game that Carter-Vickers is not going to be available for. And Celtic could have done with his experience on the day. Celtic Tipped to Make January Move for 29-Year-Old Goalkeeper Celtic have been tipped to make a January move for the 29-year-old goalkeeper, amid the club's recent struggles. Who will start at centre-back for Celtic vs Celta Vigo? Dane Murray earned a lot of praise for his performance against Hearts at the weekend. So, it is quite likely that he is going to be the one starting against Celta Vigo as well. On the other hand, it might be a toss-up between Auston Trusty and Liam Scales in the other centre-back position. Trusty had played the entire 90 minutes against Benfica, while Scales did the same against Hearts. So, it does look like O'Neill wants to stick to the left-footed, right-footed centre-back combination. If you asked me, Scales is most likely to retain his place in the starting XI after the one-sided win against Hearts. When it comes to Trusty, his combination with Murray did not really work when the two started against Benfica last week. The Celtic defence proved too easy to get through for the Portuguese side, who scored four goals and could have easily had a few more if they had been a bit more clinical with their finishing. Then again, one cannot rule out the possibility of O'Neill deciding to rely on experience and going with the Scales-Trusty duo, which was his preferred setup for most of his last season.
