item.title: Honda confirms Diogo Moreira for factory team in 2027; David Alonso heads to LCR
item.description: Motorsport photo Honda confirmed on Tuesday that Diogo Moreira will join the manufacturer’s factory MotoGP team next season, where he will partner Fabio Quartararo . The announcement means that David Alonso, who agreed a deal with HRC months ago for a promotion to the premier class for 2027, will instead join LCR, the Japanese manufacturer’s satellite team, taking the seat that will be vacated by the Brazilian. In his debut MotoGP season, reigning Moto2 world champion Moreira has delivered on the brief he was given. Not only has he proved highly consistent for much of the campaign, but he has also sent out signals that have caught the attention of Honda’s Japanese executives. The Sao Paulo-born rider sits 15th in the overall standings – and is Honda’s second-highest-placed rider, behind Luca Marini , who has scored 34 more points than him. So far this season, Moreira has finished inside the top 10 on five occasions, with sixth place in Hungary and second in the Motegi sprint standing out as his most notable results. Initially, Moreira is expected to work alongside crew chief Andres Madrid, who will join HRC from KTM, while Santi Hernandez, who heads up Joan Mir ’s side of the garage, will oversee Alonso’s adaptation to the premier class. “It’s an amazing feeling to join the factory team; it’s something every rider dreams of when they are young. I want to thank everyone at HRC for believing in me and giving me the opportunity to take the next step in this project,” Moreira said in Honda’s official statement. David Alonso David Alonso Honda’s decision to back Moreira appears entirely justified when his performances are compared with those of Alonso, the other candidate to become Quartararo’s team-mate. The Colombian, who dominated Moto3 in 2024, began his second Moto2 campaign aiming to fight for the title, but that target has gradually slipped away as the season has progressed. His sole victory, at Assen, and four podium finishes have left him fifth in the standings, 99.5 points behind Manuel Gonzalez, who is likely to contest the intermediate-class title with Izan Guevara, currently just 5.5 points behind him. Despite Alonso’s lack of winning form, Honda gave considerable thought to assigning him to Lucio Cecchinello’s team. One of the reasons was the pressure it faced from the Wasserman Group, the agency representing the Colombian, which consistently pushed for him to be placed in the factory team. That position ran counter to the view held by several influential figures within Honda, who felt the pressure Alonso would face in his rookie season in the premier class would be excessive. item.title: Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho to keenly study Barcelona vs PSG ahead of El Clasico
item.description: Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho to keenly study Barcelona vs PSG ahead of El Clasico According to a report from SPORT , it has come to light that Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho will closely analyse Barcelona’s Champions League meeting with Paris Saint-Germain in order to prepare for the El Clasico. The Portuguese manager is particularly interested in how Hansi Flick reorganises his defence amid injury concerns , believing Tuesday’s European showdown could reveal important clues about Barcelona’s plans for the meeting at the Spotify Camp Nou. Mourinho is not yet shifting his full attention towards the Clasico, with Real Madrid’s own European commitments taking priority. However, once that fixture is out of the way, he and his coaching staff will turn their focus to assessing Barcelona’s performance against Luis Enrique’s PSG. Barcelona’s defensive absences could influence Mourinho’s Clasico plan The availability of Jules Kounde and Eric Garcia is expected to be a major focus of Mourinho’s analysis. Both defenders have featured on Barcelona’s right side this season, and their absence leaves Flick facing important decisions over how to assemble his back line for two demanding matches. Mourinho will pay close attention to Barcelona’s UCL match against PSG. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images) The Portuguese coach already knows Barcelona’s strengths and attacking patterns well. Nevertheless, the PSG match offers a valuable opportunity to see how Flick responds when key defensive options are unavailable against a high-level opponent. Mourinho will inevitably be interested in those adjustments, but Barcelona should also view the match as an opportunity to demonstrate that their system can withstand personnel changes. A disciplined performance would strengthen Flick’s options and give Real Madrid less reason to believe the absences represent an exploitable weakness. Kounde’s possible return offers Barcelona hope There remains a possibility that Kounde could recover in time to feature against Real Madrid, giving Flick greater flexibility ahead of the Clasico. His availability would be significant because it could allow Barcelona to restore a familiar defensive combination rather than rely on an emergency solution. Jules Kounde might return for El Clasico. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images) The team selected against PSG may therefore provide only part of the picture. If Kounde remains unavailable, however, Flick’s choices in Paris could offer an indication of his preferred alternatives. At the same time, if the Frenchman returns for Sunday, Barcelona’s defensive setup could look considerably different. The priority for Barça will be managing the situation without taking unnecessary risks with players’ fitness. Two demanding fixtures in quick succession make squad management especially important, and Flick will need to balance European needs with the importance of the domestic showdown.

item.title: Exeter City captain Fitzwater extends deal to 2029
item.description: Jack Fitzwater has started all 11 of Exeter City's League Two games this season [Shutterstock] Exeter captain Jack Fitzwater has extended his contract with the League One side until the summer of 2029. The 29-year-old centre-back took over as skipper in the summer after fellow defender Pierce Sweeney left the club. Having joined the Grecians in the summer of 2023 from Scottish side Livingston, he has gone on to make 77 appearances and has been a key part of a defence that has only conceded a League Two-best six goals in 11 games. Fitzwater has been a regular in the Exeter side since overcoming ulcerative colitis, which he was diagnosed with during his first season at St James Park. He had previously been contracted to the club until next summer. Fitzwater's pride at becoming Exeter City captain 'I was embarrassed going to the toilet 30 times a day' Fitzwater signs new Exeter City contract "I want to be a big part of the future and what the club is building, both on and off the pitch," Fitzwater told the club website. "I think it's a good place of change right now, and there is only one place we want to go, and that's forwards and upwards. I really want to be a big part of that. "I'm captain of the club now as well, which comes with that added responsibility. Me and my wife are happy and settled in the area, and we've made Exeter our home. We absolutely love it down here. "That's a big thing for the next few years and is a massive part of it. If you're happy off the pitch, then hopefully it helps you perform on the pitch as well." All the latest Exeter City news

item.title: Niko Kovac adamant Borussia Dortmund not in crisis
item.description: Niko Kovac adamant Borussia Dortmund not in crisis Borussia Dortmund haven’t won any games since the end of the lengthy international break. However, head coach Niko Kovac believes the team is far from crisis. Speaking ahead of the UEFA Champions League game against Sabah Baku , the 55-year-old coach said , “When we arrived back then, we were eleventh. You can’t compare the two. We’re second, level on points with Bayern. I can put that into perspective. We dominated Bremen, had an unfortunate 2–2 draw, and now against Union it was a clear 0–0 game. What we’re not entirely happy with are the results. Two draws and one defeat, but I’m not making a big deal out of it.” Kovac believes the team will be able to turn results around as soon as possible: “The team has the quality to turn things round as early as tomorrow, and I’m convinced of that. So, I’ll stick to it: read nothing. That’s the easiest and best way to go about it.” With the recent run of poor results, doubts are resurfacing about Kovac. The coach recently extended his stay at BVB until 2029 , with fans divided on whether the new contract was the right decision. Tuesday night’s game is an opportunity to get back to winning ways, as anything other than all three points will possibly increase the discontent around the club. GGFN | Brook Genene

item.title: ‘He Ain’t Wrong,’ ‘This Is Why He Doesn’t Have An Extension’ — NFL Fans Split as Troy Aikman Claims Analytics Can Cost HCs Their Jobs on MNF Broadcast
item.description: Nov 3, 2025; Arlington, Texas, USA; Monday Night Football commentator Troy Aikman before the game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Arizona Cardinals at AT&T Stadium. © Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Troy Aikman has been a popular conversation piece these last few weeks, mostly because it’s public knowledge that he’s in the final year of his broadcasting contract with ESPN and has had no negotiations with the four-letter network about an extension. Meanwhile, his long-time broadcast partner, Joe Buck, recently signed a six-year extension, keeping him around until 2032. On Week 6 Monday Night Football, the focus was back on Aikman’s analysis as the San Francisco 49ers picked up a 23-17 win over the Washington Commanders. It wasn’t anything that would get the Hall of Fame quarterback in trouble, but it sure has generated quite a bit of discussion. Troy Aikman’s Take on Analytics Splits Opinion Down the Middle Analytics have become a huge part of sports, including the NFL. But don’t tell that to Aikman, who clearly doesn’t think highly of the trend. Case in point, during the “Monday Night Football” broadcast, Aikman said, “ I think analytics is a good way to lose your job as a head coach .” That may be true, but it could also be a great way to improve a coach’s win-loss record if they can master their situational awareness. Not everyone agreed with Aikman’s assessment of analytics. One commenter simply said, “ This is why he doesn’t have an extension .” Another piggybacked off that take, “ Says the commenter about to lose his job .” DIVE IN: PFN’s Free NFL HQ — Team and Player Stats, Info, and More Yet, others agreed. One commenter said, “ He ain’t wrong .” Another defended Aikman for being willing to share his opinion, even if it is unpopular with some. “ He’s free to have his own opinion , it is literally his job to give it. Weird how defensive people are about analytics.” Another urged Aikman to “ keep speaking your mind .” However, one commenter suggested the opposite of what Aikman said is true. “Actually it’s usually the opposite . Most of the time analytics give coaches cover with their numbers-obsessed owner overlords. Going with your gut exposes you.” However, another argument was made that it’s not actually relying on analytics that gets anyone fired; it’s simply the act of losing games rather than winning them. “ Nobody gets fired for going for it . They get fired for losing, and the list of coaches who punted their way into unemployment on fourth and short is a lot longer than the list of analytics casualties.” Ultimately, this feels like one of those battles that will lead to a split opinion. Can analytics help make more informed decisions? Absolutely. But blindly following them can also get a coach in trouble. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Why the Rays don’t have what it takes to beat Brewers in the World Series
item.description: Nick Turchiaro-Imagn Images. Why the Rays don’t have what it takes to beat Brewers in the World Series appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Tampa Bay Rays have earned their place in the World Series. But earning a chance at a championship and having the tools to finish the job are two different things. Against the Milwaukee Brewers , the Rays face an opponent better prepared to win the moments that matter most. Milwaukee’s biggest advantage is its bullpen. Through eight postseason games, Brewers relievers have posted a 1.33 ERA. That kind of reliability changes the way a team approaches October baseball. When a starter falters or a close game reaches the late innings, Milwaukee can turn to fresh arms without surrendering control. Tampa Bay’s starters may keep games tight, but that only makes the strength of the Brewers’ relief corps more important. Rest adds another layer to that edge. The Brewers swept the Los Angeles Dodgers in four games to reach the World Series, while Tampa Bay needed six to get past the Cleveland Guardians. Extra days off do not guarantee sharper performances, but they give the Brewers more flexibility to manage their pitchers and prepare for situations. Over a seven-game series, those decisions can make all the difference. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Brewers also have the more dangerous offensive approach. They are capable of extending at-bats, getting runners aboard and applying pressure without waiting for one dramatic swing. Against the Rays’ rotation, that patience could be crucial. Even excellent pitchers eventually have to work through traffic, and Milwaukee has shown it can capitalize when opportunities appear. Then there is home-field advantage. The Brewers finished 103-59, compared with Tampa Bay’s 98-64, earning the right to host the opening two games and, if necessary, the final two. In a matchup that could turn on a handful of pitches, playing those pivotal games in Milwaukee matters. None of this means the Rays are completely overmatched. Drew Rasmussen and Freddy Peralta anchor Tampa Bay’s starting pitching , and the team’s ability to survive a championship series deserves respect. Junior Caminero and Yandy Diaz can change a game with one swing. The Rays have already proved they can withstand pressure. But surviving pressure is different from controlling it. The Brewers have the deeper late-inning options, a rested pitching staff, an offense built to create chances and the benefit of its home crowd when the stakes rise. The Rays have enough talent to challenge the Brewers, but Milwaukee’s depth, experience and versatility give it the edge in crucial moments. Tampa Bay will fight until the end, but Milwaukee has everything it needs to finish the job in six games. Related: Brewers’ sweeping of Dodgers sets new NLCS viewership record not seen in 11 years
item.content:encoded: Nick Turchiaro-Imagn Images. Why the Rays don’t have what it takes to beat Brewers in the World Series appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Tampa Bay Rays have earned their place in the World Series. But earning a chance at a championship and having the tools to finish the job are two different things. Against the Milwaukee Brewers , the Rays face an opponent better prepared to win the moments that matter most. Milwaukee’s biggest advantage is its bullpen. Through eight postseason games, Brewers relievers have posted a 1.33 ERA. That kind of reliability changes the way a team approaches October baseball. When a starter falters or a close game reaches the late innings, Milwaukee can turn to fresh arms without surrendering control. Tampa Bay’s starters may keep games tight, but that only makes the strength of the Brewers’ relief corps more important. Rest adds another layer to that edge. The Brewers swept the Los Angeles Dodgers in four games to reach the World Series, while Tampa Bay needed six to get past the Cleveland Guardians. Extra days off do not guarantee sharper performances, but they give the Brewers more flexibility to manage their pitchers and prepare for situations. Over a seven-game series, those decisions can make all the difference. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Brewers also have the more dangerous offensive approach. They are capable of extending at-bats, getting runners aboard and applying pressure without waiting for one dramatic swing. Against the Rays’ rotation, that patience could be crucial. Even excellent pitchers eventually have to work through traffic, and Milwaukee has shown it can capitalize when opportunities appear. Then there is home-field advantage. The Brewers finished 103-59, compared with Tampa Bay’s 98-64, earning the right to host the opening two games and, if necessary, the final two. In a matchup that could turn on a handful of pitches, playing those pivotal games in Milwaukee matters. None of this means the Rays are completely overmatched. Drew Rasmussen and Freddy Peralta anchor Tampa Bay’s starting pitching , and the team’s ability to survive a championship series deserves respect. Junior Caminero and Yandy Diaz can change a game with one swing. The Rays have already proved they can withstand pressure. But surviving pressure is different from controlling it. The Brewers have the deeper late-inning options, a rested pitching staff, an offense built to create chances and the benefit of its home crowd when the stakes rise. The Rays have enough talent to challenge the Brewers, but Milwaukee’s depth, experience and versatility give it the edge in crucial moments. Tampa Bay will fight until the end, but Milwaukee has everything it needs to finish the job in six games. Related: Brewers’ sweeping of Dodgers sets new NLCS viewership record not seen in 11 years

item.title: The best quotes about Eric Cantona
item.description: The best quotes about Eric Cantona Eric Cantona remains one of the Premier League 's most impactful footballers. Cantona was the signing that proved to be the catalyst behind Manchester United 's dominance of the division, helping break the club's long title wait before taking over the league. Having helped Leeds United to the title in the final pre-Premier League campaign, a chance conversation between the rivals saw Cantona move to Manchester, and the landscape of English football shift. Cantona won four titles in five seasons at Manchester United, and possessed an unmissable, unmatched presence. His trademark upturned collar, puffed-out chest, and ability to conjure moments of magic, remain etched into the minds of fans from that era. Cantona came, saw, and conquered with signature swagger. An icon of the Premier League , here are some of the best tributes towards the French forward. The best tributes to Eric Cantona "If ever there was one player, anywhere in the world, that was made for Manchester United, it was Cantona. He swaggered in, stuck his chest out, raised his head and surveyed everything as though he were asking: ‘I’m Cantona. How big are you? Are you big enough for me?'” - Sir Alex Ferguson “In my eyes, he was responsible for the Premier League developing as quickly as it did. Everyone took to him, controversy or not. He oozed charisma and genius in equal measure, and is by far and away the best ever in the Premier League. It was an honour to have played with him.” - Peter Schmeichel “Collar up, back straight, chest stuck out, he glided into the arena as if he owned the f***ing place. Any arena, but nowhere more effectively than Old Trafford. This was his stage. He loved it, the crowd loved him.” - Roy Keane “When Cantona did come to United I knew that we’d win the title because he just had the aura and presence about him. He took the responsibility away from all of us lot. He was unbelievable." - Paul Ince “What hasn’t already been said about Eric Cantona? A sublime player, and the guy who opened the door for so many other Frenchmen in the English championship. A player with character – the King!” - Emmanuel Petit “Once he got to United, everything changed. It was as if he’d found the place he belonged and the stage he thought he deserved." - David Beckham “Eric Cantona (also) brought an extra dimension (to Manchester United). Plenty of things he tried didn’t come off, but you remember the ones that did — the flicks, the outrageous lobs. He made things look easy that weren’t easy at all. Before him, we struggled to score as a team, but as soon as he arrived the goals flowed."

item.title: English right-back is coming to Liverpool
item.description: English right-back is coming to Liverpool An exciting right-back is coming to Liverpool's first-team. The right-back position is something the Reds have failed to figure out for a while. For close to a decade it was so easy for Liverpool. In Trent Alexander-Arnold, they had the best right-back on the planet. No one else could compete with the way he played. He was so instrumental to Liverpool's success. Alexander-Arnold made things happen with ease on the pitch. He controlled the creativity and the build-up of Jurgen Klopp's side. During his peak years he could unlock any defence and Liverpool were visibly worse when he was not playing. However, he then decided to ruin it all by saying something like - I want to join Real Madrid. With that declaration it was all over. He left Anfield on a free transfer in what has been a terrible move for every party involved. Could Trent come back to Liverpool? The reality is that Liverpool still haven't replaced him. They've tried with Jeremie Frimpong but he simply isn't good enough. Dominik Szoboszlai doesn't want to play there and Ronald Araujo is solid but he is a temporary solution. Meanwhile, things have not worked out for Alexander-Arnold either. He arrived at Real Madrid wanting to win trophies and personal accolades like the Ballon d'Or. Instead he's found himself in a troubled Madrid side with Barcelona dominating and Alexander-Arnold mostly sitting on the bench. He's had three managers now and none of them have made him their first-choice right-back. It doesn't make sense for Madrid to be paying him high wages and for him to be spending his prime years sitting on the bench. But a return to Liverpool would have to hinge on a lot of things. A reasonable transfer fee, and probably reduced wages. Alexander-Arnold might not want to take that, and perhaps neither will Real Madrid. Liverpool's new English right-back - Ollie O'Connor With the injury to Jeremie Frimpong, the Reds are now without a recognised back-up right-back which means there's an opportunity for a youngster from the academy to join the first-team. And that means Ollie O'Connor will now likely be heading to Andoni Iraola's team for the next few games until Frimpong is back fit. Why? Well, O'Connor is Liverpool's best right-back at U21 level. He's caught the eye in EFL Trophy games against senior opposition and he has all the characteristics you need to make it at a high level. O'Connor is hard-working, he covers a lot of ground and he never gives up. The Englishman is someone who Andoni Iraola will enjoy working with.

item.title: Jayden Daniels Has Message After Near-Comeback Against 49ers
item.description: Jayden Daniels Commanders 49ers Getty Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels sent a clear message after the team’s near-comeback against the San Francisco 49ers. The 49ers took a 20-3 lead into halftime, and it appeared that the game would be out of reach for the Commanders. But Daniels and his team played a strong second half, cutting the deficit to 23-17 and having a chance to win the game on the final drive of the game. Ultimately, the Commanders came up short as they lost the game and dropped to 1-4-1 on the season. But Daniels was proud of the team for putting up a tough fight to make the game competitive instead of just giving up. Jayden Daniels on What Commanders Need to Do Better Speaking to reporters after the game, Daniels shared his thoughts on what the Commanders need to do better going forward so they don’t have to dig themselves out of such a massive hole in the second half of their next game. “Just one play at a time. We said that offensively; we said that as a team. Just one play at a time. We dug ourselves in a hole… we gotta be a full-game, four-quarter team, not just a half team,” Daniels said. “We just said collectively as a team, do everything one play at a time, just do your job. Don’t try to do someone else’s job, just do your job, and we just started rattling off longer drives, 3-and-outs, stuff like that.” Commanders Have Bye Week Coming Up With the Commanders now having a 1-4-1 record, the team has a bye week coming up, and it is coming up at the perfect time, as Washington could really use a break to reset things after their recent struggles. Last week, the Commanders had a very disappointing tie against the New York Giants in a game that they probably should have won , and then this week, they lost once again. Other than their upset win over the Seattle Seahawks earlier this season, the Commanders have not achieved a victory so far this year, which could put head coach Dan Quinn’s job in jeopardy. Given how well the Commanders played in the second half of this game against the 49ers, it could potentially buy Quinn more time behind the team’s sidelines, though a change at head coach cannot be completely ruled out at this time. As poor as Washington is playing, they still have a chance to make the playoffs this season just because their division is playing so poorly at the moment. The New York Giants lead the NFC East at 3-2-1, with the Philadelphia Eagles and the Dallas Cowboys each at 2-4. The Eagles also just lost QB Jalen Hurts for potentially the rest of the season, so the Commanders have an even greater chance of making a run in their division. But, as Daniels said, it all starts with one play at a time, and the Commanders need to really buy into that sort of game plan when they take on the Eagles in Week 8 following their bye week in what will certainly be a must-win game. item.title: Crystal Palace make sack decision on Pierre Sage after Brighton thrashing
item.description: Crystal Palace make sack decision on Pierre Sage after Brighton thrashing Pierre Sage is facing intense scrutiny over his future at Crystal Palace. The Eagles suffered a 5-0 thrashing at Brighton & Hove Albion on Saturday, which is the club’s heaviest defeat against their arch-rivals in 70 years. But despite the disappointing result, the club’s hierarchy plan to give Sage more time to prove himself at Selhurst Park, per The Athletic . Palace do not intend to make an immediate managerial change and the 47-year-old is expected to take charge of coming matches against Besiktas and Newcastle United. Sage was appointed as Palace manager after Oliver Glasner left in the summer. The French boss has won just two of his opening seven Premier League matches. His team has conceded the most goals (17) in the English top-flight. But there is an acknowledgement Palace are not in freefall, as they are 14th in the league with seven points. Sage has not been able to pick a consistent backline due to injuries or suspension to Chadi Riad, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Axel Disasi. The Frenchman is not out of the woods, as club chairman Steve Parish could decide to sack him if there is no sign of progress in the next two games. If Sage is dismissed, Palace could consider appointing Kieran McKenna or Frank Lampard as a replacement. McKenna has been out of work since leaving Ipswich Town at the end of last season, while Lampard is currently the head coach of Coventry City.

item.title: Irwin backs himself to bounce back after 'hard' year
item.description: Glenn Irwin is a two-time British Superbike Championship runner-up [Getty Images] Glenn Irwin believes he can return to the front of the British Superbike Championship, with an exciting move to Michael Laverty's BMW-backed team providing fresh motivation for 2027. The 12-time North West 200 Superbike race winner will ride an Alpha Racing-prepared BMW M 1000 RR for the GRYD Racing team, co-owned by Laverty and David Eltherington. The 36-year-old Northern Ireland rider admits 2026 failed to live up to expectations as injuries, crashes, technical issues and a difficult relationship with Ducati's new Panigale V4R, combined to derail his title ambitions. Despite showing flashes of his speed with a podium at Knockhill and success at the North West 200, Irwin was left searching for answers throughout a frustrating campaign and ended 14th in the series standings. The Carrickfergus rider has twice finished runner-up in BSB, including being pipped by half-a-point by then teammate Tommy Bridewell in 2023. "It's been hard," he reflected of his 2026 season on the BBC Bikes podcast. "There were moments when doubts came in, because that's natural as a sports person, but there were also moments this year when you realise you shouldn't have those doubts." Those doubts also extended to his future. After a disappointing season by his own high standards, Irwin admitted he was concerned about whether the right opportunity would emerge for 2027. However, the chance to join Michael Laverty's team alongside Englishman Storm Stacey quickly convinced him it was the fresh start he needed. "Storm's a great team-mate," added Irwin. "I'm looking forward to taking from him and also passing on to him." 'We've done it before and we can do it again' Another significant factor in Irwin's decision was the North West 200. The event remains hugely important to the county Antrim rider and he wanted a package capable of competing at the front in both British Superbikes and road racing. BMW's proven strength around the NW200 circuit, coupled with Stacey's impressive performances there, made the move even more appealing. While excitement surrounds the new challenge, Irwin is under no illusions about what lies ahead, although he does believe the combination of experience, renewed confidence and a fresh start can help him fight his way back to winning ways. "Of course, you have to perform," he said. "The whippersnappers are coming up through and you can either step aside and let them take your job or you can fight. "You look at people like Leon Haslam and Tommy Bridewell. You can continue to get better in this sport. If you want to stay in it, you have to. "The expectation is there because we know what we can do. We've done it before and we can do it again."

item.title: Explained: What is BCCI-CA Umpire exchange programme as Australian umpire set to officiate Ranji Trophy matches
item.description: Explained: What is BCCI-CA Umpire exchange programme as Australian umpire set to officiate Ranji Trophy matches originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Australian umpire Ben Treloar will officiate two Ranji Trophy matches in India as part of an exchange programme between Cricket Australia and the BCCI. India umpire Parashar Joshi will stand in two Sheffield Shield matches and one One Day Cup match in Australia in November. Treloar has officiated 89 domestic matches and six women's internationals, while Joshi has officiated 91 domestic matches. Explained: What is the BCCI-CA Umpire exchange programme Cricket Australia and the BCCI have announced an exchange where each board sends one umpire to work in the other's domestic competitions. Australia's Ben Treloar is in India for two Ranji Trophy matches, while India's Parashar Joshi will umpire two Sheffield Shield games and one One Day Cup match. Treloar is already in Delhi, where he will stand in the Ranji Trophy match between Delhi and Gujarat from October 18 to 21. He then moves to Mumbai for their game against Haryana from October 26 to 29, so he will see two different cities. Joshi's tour starts with the Sheffield Shield match between Queensland and Tasmania at the Gabba from November 11 to 14, followed by their One Day Cup game at the same venue on November 16. He finishes with New South Wales against Queensland at the SCG from November 22 to 25. The idea behind such an exchange is to give umpires exposure to different playing conditions and competition structures and to strengthen the working relationship between the two boards. The announcement does not say when the programme began, or how many umpires will take part in future. MORE: BCCI confirms Agarkar replacement: Explaining why Powar failed to trump Ojha for India Chief Selector role Ben Treloar and Parashar Joshi: How many matches have they officiated? Treloar has officiated 30 First-Class matches, 20 List A matches and 39 Big Bash League games, which adds up to 89 domestic matches. He has also stood in two Women's One Day Internationals and four Women's T20 Internationals, which gives him six matches at international level. Away from the field, Treloar is Cricket New South Wales' Umpire Education Officer and helps develop the next generation of match officials. His work has earned him four George Borwick Memorial Awards from the New South Wales Cricket Umpires and Scorers Association. Joshi has officiated 19 First-Class matches across the Ranji Trophy and Duleep Trophy, 32 List A matches in the Vijay Hazare Trophy and Deodhar Trophy, and 40 T20 matches. That is 91 domestic matches, including appointments in the Indian Premier League and Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy. Joshi's record does not include any international matches, so the visiting umpires differ mainly in that respect. Joshi has officiated 19 First-Class matches across the Ranji Trophy and Duleep Trophy, 32 List A matches in the Vijay Hazare Trophy and Deodhar Trophy, and 40 T20 matches. That is 91 domestic matches, including appointments in the Indian Premier League and Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy. Joshi's record does not include any international matches, so the visiting umpires differ mainly in that respect. On domestic workload, they are almost level, with Treloar on 89 matches and Joshi on 91, suggesting the pairing was built as a swap between peers. MORE: ‘(Rohit Sharma) wants that cup’: How Ojha’s appointment is good news for Indian veteran batter The umpire exchange is worth having, but only if India learns something from it The exchange is a sound idea, but one visiting umpire standing in two Ranji Trophy matches will not change Indian umpiring on its own. Exposure matters only if it leads to measurable results, but the announcement does not specify what either board hopes to see afterwards. The numbers show a swap between near equals, with Treloar on 89 domestic matches and Joshi on 91, so the real difference is Treloar's job as an umpire educator. The BCCI would gain most if he ran a session for state umpires and reviewed footage from the Delhi and Mumbai games. The same applies to Joshi, who will return from the Gabba and the SCG with experience that is useful only if the BCCI asks for it. A written report on conditions, decisions and match management in Australia would turn one man's trip into something the whole panel can use. If the boards publish what each umpire learned and widen the exchange to more officials next season, it could become a real development tool. If it ends with two match reports and a press note, it will have been a goodwill gesture and little more. To keep up to date with all the latest cricket news and share your opinion on the biggest topics, visit our Facebook , Instagram and X (Twitter) pages.

item.title: Freddy Peralta’s wild run with Rays is like no other since 1968
item.description: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images Freddy Peralta’s wild run with Rays is like no other since 1968 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . In August, the Tampa Bay Rays acquired Freddy Peralta in a trade with the New York Mets. Just a few days later, he was named AL Pitcher of the Month. Apparently, it was a sign of bigger things to come for the Rays. On Monday, Peralta and Tampa Bay reached the World Series after outclassing the Cleveland Guardians , 7-3, in Game 6 of the ALCS at Tropicana Field. The 30-year-old Peralta was named MVP of the best-of-seven series. He allowed one run on five hits with three walks and three strikeouts in 5 1/3 innings. He also led the Brewers to the win in Game 2 and recorded a hold in Game 4. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) In the process, he also achieved a rare milestone , according to OptaSTATS. “Freddy Peralta over his last 10 appearances dating back to the regular season: 50.0+ total IP, one run or fewer allowed in all 10, and the team won all 10,” read the post on X. “The last two MLB pitchers to do that over a stretch of 10 appearances (regular/postseason) were Bob Gibson (1968) and Walter Johnson (1913).” Freddy Peralta over his last 10 appearances dating back to the regular season: 50.0+ total IP 1 run or fewer allowed in all 10 team won all 10 The last 2 MLB pitchers to do that over a stretch of 10 appearances (reg/post) were Bob Gibson (1968) & Walter Johnson (1913). pic.twitter.com/Mcq6889wux — OptaSTATS (@OptaSTATS) October 20, 2026 Gibson starred for the St. Louis Cardinals, while Johnson played for the Washington Senators. Both won a championship. Peralta has peaked at the perfect time for the Rays, who sent Aidan Smith, Gary Gill Hill, and Emilien Pitre to the Mets to acquire the two-time All-Star. He reached the World Series for the first time and is set to face his former team, the Milwaukee Brewers, who signed him in 2018. The Rays advanced to the Fall Classic for the first time since 2020. Related: Why the Rays don’t have what it takes to beat Brewers in the World Series Related: Rays’ Junior Caminero explains his perfect Randy Arozarena tribute in ALCS Game 6

item.title: CTA explains why Real Madrid’s Arda Guler cannot be punished for Sevilla incident
item.description: CTA explains why Real Madrid’s Arda Guler cannot be punished for Sevilla incident The Spanish Technical Committee of Referees (CTA) has explained why it cannot take disciplinary action over Arda Guler’s incident against Sevilla, with the available footage failing to establish exactly how the Real Madrid midfielder made contact with Peque . The incident occurred during the first half of Real Madrid’s match against Sevilla, which was still goalless at the time. Sevilla believe Guler should have been sent off for an alleged elbow, but the lack of a conclusive camera angle has complicated any attempt to review the episode retrospectively, as per MARCA . CTA says available footage cannot establish what happened The central problem is not that the incident was missed by every camera, but that none of the available angles provides enough detail to establish precisely what happened. Sources at LaLiga told MARCA that 23 camera angles were used for the broadcast, yet only the widest views captured the confrontation. Those included a rear camera, the Skycam and the camera generally used for offside decisions. The production team did not have a closer shot that could clearly establish whether Guler struck Peque with his elbow or made contact in another way. According to the report, this was not a production error because the relevant footage simply does not exist, and the signal received by the television production was the same as that available to the VAR team. That information is quite crucial because it suggests the controversy cannot be resolved by obtaining an alternative broadcast angle that was available but unused. Simply put, the necessary visual evidence was never captured in sufficient detail. VAR cannot intervene without conclusive evidence Sources from the CTA explained why the available images do not provide a basis for further action. They stressed that not every camera at a match is suitable for VAR purposes, particularly when an incident happens away from the ball and outside the referee’s immediate field of view. CTA cannot intervene in the Arda Guler incident. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) “Of the many cameras at the match, not all are suitable for VAR. The incident took place behind the referee, in an area away from the ball. “The cameras weren’t focused there; only those with a very wide angle were. As we’ve seen, the incident is visible, but there’s no detail.” The same sources emphasised that the images do not establish the nature of the contact or provide enough evidence to justify retrospective intervention. “It’s not clear whether he hit him with his shoulder, his elbow or his hand, in the face… You can’t see. “And as there is no evidence, no action can be taken. No penalty was given on the pitch and VAR, without conclusive evidence, cannot do anything,” it stated.

item.title: Former Auburn Linebacker Xavier Atkins breaks silence after dismissal
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Randy Sartin-Imagn Images Former Auburn Linebacker Xavier Atkins breaks silence after dismissal appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Former Auburn Tigers linebacker Xavier Atkins has officially broken his silence following his sudden dismissal from the college football program on Monday. The star defensive playmaker was previously suspended ahead of Auburn’s massive upset victory over the then-No. 1 Georgia Bulldogs, leaving his status in limbo before head coach Alex Golesh made the final decision to remove him from the roster. Addressing his departure publicly for the first time, Atkins released a statement expressing respect for the school while laying out his immediate priorities moving forward. “I have nothing but respect Auburn University and will continue to support my teammates this season,” Atkins stated. “My focus is on my health, my family, and on finishing up the academic semester strong, and I’ll be entering the transfer portal at the appropriate time.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Losing Atkins leaves a massive hole in the middle of the Auburn defense. Before his internal suspension, the junior linebacker was putting together another strong campaign. Through five games this season, Atkins tallied 37 tackles, three sacks, seven tackles for loss, and one interception for the Tigers. His early 2026 production followed a dominant 2025 season where he established himself as one of college football’s premier linebackers. Atkins earned First-Team All-SEC and All-American honors last year after leading the conference with 17 tackles for loss while adding 84 total tackles and nine sacks. The Auburn Tigers managed to pull off a thrilling win over top-ranked Georgia without their defensive anchor, but losing a talent like Atkins creates a huge challenge for Golesh’s defense as SEC play heats up. Atkins originally began his collegiate career with the LSU Tigers before transferring to Auburn and emerging as a defensive star. Now, the talented linebacker plans to complete his academic requirements and focus on his personal wellbeing before searching for his next college home when the transfer portal opens. Related: Urban Meyer calls out ‘perplexing’ Ohio State’s Ryan Day QB decision Related: Auburn make final decision on suspended linebacker Xavier Atkins

item.title: 🗞️ A gala night in Paris: Tuesday's front pages
item.description: 🗞️ A gala night in Paris: Tuesday's front pages The front pages of Europe's sports newspapers this Tuesday, October 20, focus on a thrilling day of Champions League action, with the clash between PSG and Barcelona taking centre stage. Meanwhile, in Italy, pressure is mounting on the Juventus manager, while in Portugal, Cristiano Ronaldo's disciplinary case has been resolved. The Parc des Princes hosts the 'Euroclásico' The showdown between Paris Saint-Germain and FC Barcelona is the day's headline fixture. Newspapers such as Marca (Blockbuster amid unrest), Mundo Deportivo (Euroclásico), Sport (Gala match) and France's L'Équipe (We want more) and Le Figaro (Clash of titans) highlight the magnitude of the encounter between Luis Enrique's and Hansi Flick's sides. Despite tension over security incidents near the Paris stadium, which prompted police unions to request a postponement, reassurances from the French authorities mean the match will go ahead. Both managers head into the game having exchanged praise, although Barça are hampered by significant absences in defence. Juventus struggling; Serie A demands goals In Italy, attention turns to the difficult situation at Juventus, both on and off the pitch. Both La Gazzetta dello Sport (Spalletti on the brink) and Corriere dello Sport ( Lucio and shadows) reflect the deep crisis engulfing the Turin club after a shaky start to the season. With Luciano Spalletti 's future in doubt following the setback against Lazio , fans are beginning to call for Antonio Conte 's return. The Italian newspapers are also urging teams such as Napoli and Roma to respond on the European stage to secure qualification. Cristiano Ronaldo's suspension confirmed In Portugal, the news centres on the outcome of the disciplinary proceedings opened against Cristiano Ronaldo after he left the national team camp. Both A Bola (CR7 in Jesus's hands) and Record (Ronaldo free for Jesus) report the ruling by the Portuguese Football Federation's Disciplinary Council: a 30-day suspension and a €255 fine. Having already served most of the ban under a provisional suspension, the Portugal captain will complete his suspension before the end of the month, leaving his possible return for November's fixtures in the hands of national team coach Jorge Jesus. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇪🇸 here.

item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Villarreal’s Iñigo Pérez ready to meet Iraola again in test of old bond
item.description: Refused a work permit at Bournemouth, Pérez comes face to face with Liverpool’s head coach in Champions League On Iñigo Pérez’s first day as a head coach he took a call from Andoni Iraola, just as he had every day for months. They had known each other for 22 years, lived in the same residency, come through the same academy and played in the same team; they had worked side by side, manager and assistant, and embarked on an adventure together. Now, though, Pérez was having to go it alone. At 36, he had become what his friend thought he would be from the moment they met, just not so soon. “He wished me luck and said he was there for me,” Pérez said, “said that if I ever needed anything …” Well, maybe not anything . Continue reading...

item.title: Where to watch Duke vs. Tennessee basketball: Channel, live stream, time, TV schedule for men's exhibition game
item.description: Where to watch Duke vs. Tennessee basketball: Channel, live stream, time, TV schedule for men's exhibition game originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . A blockbuster exhibition matchup will take place in Durham this week as No. 2 Duke hosts No. 8 Tennessee. Though it's early days, Duke is already shaping up to be a championship-level team. The Blue Devils started out on a positive note, routing Belmont 102-62 at home last week, but Tennessee will be the squad's first real test. item.title: Bayern Munich’s Jonas Urbig believes teammate Harry Kane should win the Ballon d’Or
item.description: Kane is the man of the moment. (Photo by Hesham Elsherif/Anadolu via Getty Images) | Anadolu via Getty Images Bayern Munich’s Jonas Urbig has said it. So have Declan Rice, Jude Bellingham, Michael Olise, Morgan Rogers, Luis Diaz, and Joshua Kimmich. And countless football pundits and former legends. Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane should win the Ballon d’Or later this month. He absolutely has to. There is no player more deserving of it for the 2025/26 season. Harry Kane has had the highest-scoring season EVER by a player not named Lionel Messi, making his campaign the second-best goal-scoring season of all time. He has also been integral to England’s third-place finish in the World Cup, contributing 6 goals and an assist. Bayern Munich goalkeeper and teammate Jonas Urbig revealed in a recent interview (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ) that he believes Harry Kane deserves the Ballon d’Or. When asked to elaborat e, he responded, “He does both things on both ends of the pitch – he sc ores goals non-stop, he defends, goes into duels, [and] distributes the ball. He’s everywhere on the pitch; he runs a lot. He’s an incredible footballer, [and] an incredible person. We’re so happy to have him in our team.” Word. There isn’t a player more complete than Harry Kane in world football. His ability to play across a plethora of positions and contribute to the team’s build-up and structure with his defending, his midfield positioning and passing, and the way he sprays balls out wide for the wingers to collect—all while scoring a boa tload of goals in the process—nobody does this in wo rld football quite like Kane. item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo receives 30-day suspension and £215 fine over Portugal walkout
item.description: Disciplinary council upholds charge against 41-year-old Fifa suspends Egypt’s Hossam Hassan and Mostafa Ziko Cristiano Ronaldo has been suspended for 30 days by the Portuguese ⁠FA after leaving the national team camp following a rift with the coach, ⁠Jorge Jesus, over ⁠his role in the side. The federation’s disciplinary council said it had upheld the charge against ⁠the 41-year-old forward in full and imposed a fine of €255 (£215). Ronaldo left Portugal’s base in ⁠Copenhagen before their Nations League match against Denmark this month, having accused ‌Jesus of twice ‌breaking his word about his role after he was an ‌unused substitute against Norway. item.title: Houdini act in Venice leaves Massimiliano Allegri searching for an escape at Napoli | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Manager’s latest setback exposed growing doubts about his squad and his approach as Davide Nicola began his Venezia tenure with a remarkable win “I’ll love you even if you win,” promised the Venezia supporter’s banner. More gallows humour from a fanbase that proved long ago that its relationship with the club could survive a defeat. They had endured six already in the first six rounds of this Serie A season: the only team in the division without a win or even a single point. The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th. The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom. Deja vu all over again? A 3-1 defeat by Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Leaving England is scary but I’m here to win’: Charlie Cresswell on Ligue 1 life and his international dream
item.description: Young centre-back could not see a way forward at Leeds so moved to France. Now he’s preparing for the biggest game of his life against Juventus By Get French Football News “Leaving England is such a scary, scary decision,” says Charlie Cresswell. It is a decision that he never thought he would make. His father, Richard, made a career as a footballer in England; his brother, Alfie, was coming through Leeds’s academy; Charlie was on the fringes of the Leeds first team when the opportunity to join Toulouse arose in 2024. “That was the biggest decision I made in football,” he says. “I’ve been a Leeds fan since I was eight. I’d been at the club since I was 10, but, looking back, I was 20 years old with no games and I needed to get out and go play,” says Cresswell, now at Rennes and preparing to face Juventus in the Europa League. Continue reading...

item.title: Konsa bullish about Arsenal’s Champions League hopes as Bayern clash looms
item.description: Centre-back has settled right in at Arsenal and is looking ‘to win everything’, starting with Wednesday’s duel against Harry Kane For Ezri Konsa, it was just a wonderfully satisfying challenge. The Nottingham Forest striker Liam Delap had stolen in behind him up the inside left channel on Sunday. There were 93 minutes gone, Arsenal were 1-0 up and it was now or never for Forest. Konsa decreed that it would be never, curving his covering run back, matching Delap for pace and stretching into the perfect block tackle. So, another win for Arsenal : their 10th in 11 matches this season. Another clean sheet. And for Konsa, a continuation of what has been a dreamlike couple of months. Do points-saving last-minute challenges mean more when the defender is actually a fan of the club, too? Basically, yes. Continue reading...

item.title: Semenyo’s eight-week injury absence leaves Manchester City short on cover for Haaland
item.description: Ghana forward sustained knee injury against Ipswich Maresca to ring changes against AEK Athens on Tuesday Antoine Semenyo has been ruled out for eight weeks with a knee injury, leaving Enzo Maresca short of alternatives to Erling Haaland, who is a doubt for Manchester City’s Champions League game at home against AEK Athens on Tuesday. Semenyo limped off against Ipswich on Saturday and Haaland hobbled off at full time with a foot injury. City are eager to get their European campaign back on track after losing against Paris Saint-Germain last Wednesday. item.content:encoded: Ghana forward sustained knee injury against Ipswich Maresca to ring changes against AEK Athens on Tuesday Antoine Semenyo has been ruled out for eight weeks with a knee injury, leaving Enzo Maresca short of alternatives to Erling Haaland, who is a doubt for Manchester City’s Champions League game at home against AEK Athens on Tuesday. Semenyo limped off against Ipswich on Saturday and Haaland hobbled off at full time with a foot injury. City are eager to get their European campaign back on track after losing against Paris Saint-Germain last Wednesday. Maresca has said he will make changes and has admitted previously that Haaland will require resting at some point. Semenyo would have been the most obvious replacement but Phil Foden and Iliman Ndiaye could be utilised. Continue reading...

item.title: Bayern and Luis Díaz warm up for Arsenal revenge mission with furious rout of Leipzig | Andy Brassell
item.description: Bruised Bundesliga champions hit a supposed rival for six and their flying winger is peaking at a perfect moment When Bayern Munich fail to win for two games in a row, you know what is coming next. Particularly on a Saturday night showcase, against the sort of good domestic opposition that tend to bring the best out of the champions. It had been a frustrating week, domestically and continentally, in two games on the road. On both occasions they had been caught cold, conceding the Bundesliga’s fastest goal at Augsburg and going 1-0 down in less than 90 seconds in Stavanger . Vincent Kompany’s low profile on the Allianz Arena touchline, almost motionless in his seat as his team rattled a flurry of goals past poor RB Leipzig, had nothing to do with any lingering chagrin connected to those slow starts from his team. The sporting director, Max Eberl, who stood in for his coach in the post-match press conference, explained that the Belgian had been ill, not to mention Kompany’s current hip problem that had made the move from dressing room to pitchside slow and uncomfortable. Continue reading...

item.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘I suffer a lot’: Villarreal owner Fernando Roig on not enjoying games and the prospect of Liverpool | Sid Lowe
item.description: It will be a tense time for Europe’s longest serving president, despite the Champions League game at Anfield offering a symbol of how far they have come The first time Fernando Roig watched Villarreal play as their president, he sat in the stand at a tiny whitewashed ground that had concrete fever and was half empty. It was a Sunday night in the second division, they lost 3-0 against Badajoz, and he didn’t enjoy it much. But then, he never enjoys it much. Even on Tuesday at Anfield, he will not: into his 30th year, the longest presidency in Europe, that is about the only thing that hasn’t changed. More than 1,000 games and still it happens. “I don’t get nervous,” he says. “It’s worse: I get worried, very anxious. I suffer a lot. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Haaland helps Maresca achieve record start as Manchester City defeat Ipswich
item.description: There have been few winners in Manchester City’s guilty verdict, except highly paid lawyers and the inflatable fruit industry. The fans have suffered, being forced to question everything they have been told, while being labelled “cheats”, but they were able to forget the cacophony of noise around the club as Enzo Maresca became the first Premier League manager to win his first seven games. Ipswich were the latest victims, but they put up a fight in City’s first home Premier League game since being found to have breached financial rules . Defiance has fortified most of the City fanbase, who were able to see local boy Phil Foden instigate the triumph with a kiss of the badge, before an emblem of their wealth, Erling Haaland, secured the points to move six clear, albeit with a few scares between, courtesy of Daizen Maeda and Zian Flemming. Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Watford, a ‘fake news’ sacking and an apology to Elton John
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! There are only two things certain in life – death and taxes Reece James knack and Watford managerial news – and Football Daily’s bingo card lit up with both on Friday. But while Chelsea’s statement on their crocked right-back having successful knee surgery was a cut-and-paste job from the last time James was injured, the quotes by Watford manager Alessio Dionisi were much more exciting, mainly because it contained an actual apology to Elton John and the remarkable news that the club’s trigger-happy owners have not already sent the Italian the same way as an apple in Michael Owen’s house . Shall we just hand over the Bigger Cup to PSG now to ease the calendar congestion?” – Krishna Moorthy. Reading that ‘European football leaders are increasingly confident they will find a candidate to stand against Infantino next year’ , I can’t be the only well informed reader to think that a certain intergalactic bin wearing member of the nobility would make a terrific candidate. Can the Big Website ‘Higher Ups’ have a word?!” – Chris Reid. Looking at the Benfica v Celtic game I was immediately drawn to the presence of two Durans. Have there been any other instances of any other bands being present in a game? Possibly in the Human League? I am hoping a Serie A game with a Scritti and a Politti … a French game with Depeche and Mode. You get the general idea” – Mike Turney. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: FC Copenhagen Women have a ‘startup-like’ brand. Now they need results
item.description: A famous name and record attendances have given FCK a platform but a difficult start in Denmark’s top-flight shows success on the pitch is not guaranteed On an August day in 2024, 5,165 fans gathered at Vanløse Idrætspark to watch FC Copenhagen (FCK) take on B73 Slagelse in their first league match. For Denmark’s most successful men’s club, with 16 league titles, it marked the realisation of their desire to establish a women’s team, through collaboration with the existing FC Damsø, and an ambitious project with aims of having a wide-reaching impact on and off the pitch. The 26 months since have brought a whirlwind of success, the club securing back-to-back promotions to reach the A-Liga. Now they are in the top division and “playing with the big dogs”, as their head of women’s football, Romaney Pinnock, coins it, and they must adapt to stay there. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City are suddenly box-office in age of charge-rage and mega defiance | Barney Ronay
item.description: This is by far the most interesting this club have ever been and they faced PSG, a kind of twin entity in all this as oil state glove puppets Another day, another note of unreality; another vivid and brilliant spectacle that feels as though it has been whipped together out of meringue and burnt sugar. Time flies when the world is closing in. Two weeks on, this was Manchester City’s first home game since the verdict dropped, the irrefutable body of evidence was refuted, and English football entered its state of ongoing whiplash. In the stadium this felt like watching someone dance while the world burns. This was a brilliant game pegged out around six goals , a collapse, a comeback, posts and bars struck, saved penalties, and a performance of state-of-the-art omni-football from this brilliantly high-grade Paris Saint-Germain team. Continue reading...

item.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. Continue reading...

item.title: Have any footballers ended their career with more own goals than goals? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the earliest trophyless seasons, scoring off one’s backside (part II) and the origins of ‘shithousery’ Mail us with all of your questions and answers “How many professional players have ended their senior careers with more own goals than goals for their own team?” wonders Peter Clark. In the past we’ve looked at the players with the most own goals , but we haven’t looked at those who ended their professional career in debit. “Southampton cult hero Francis Benali scored only one ‘positive’ goal in his career and was legendary for banging in goal-of-the-month contenders at his own end, most notably a bullet header against Oldham in the 1993-94 season ,” writes Daz Pearce. We could only find a couple of OGs for Benali, the other being against Manchester United in 1999-2000 . But we were unable to find a comprehensive Southampton database, so there’s a chance we’ve missed some beauties. Continue reading...

item.title: Christian Pulisic is no longer a focal point for the US or Milan – and that’s OK
item.description: The winger is 28, and younger teammates are rising into the high-pressure spots he has usually occupied Usually, the second weekend of October sees Christian Pulisic flanked by compatriots as the Star-Spangled Banner plays. Last year, he was involved in US friendlies against Ecuador and Australia. But this year, with Fifa having folded the October window into September, Pulisic didn’t have the chance. On Sunday, his pre-match music was O Generosa, the Serie A anthem, which he observed with a soft smile. Mark Twain’s first visit to Italy left him describing the country as “a vast museum of magnificence and misery”, and it’s a fitting summary of Pulisic’s three-plus years with Milan. The magnificence: 43 goals and 25 assists in 138 appearances. The misery: just one trophy since he arrived in July 2023, a 2025 Supercoppa Italia held in Saudi Arabia. Continue reading...

item.title: Winning is not enough for Manchester City to move on from this crisis | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. The majority of people involved in the game speak it with a high degree of sophistication. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. There’s an appealing quirkiness to him that suggests he has a higher-than-usual level of self-awareness. He doesn’t mind stepping outside the norms, being a bit different. But consider his assessment of Manchester City’s 3-0 win at Liverpool on Sunday. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Manchester City unrepentant in victory, Spurs make progress of a sort and Noni Madueke meets the moment The manner of Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool was an article of both vindication and vilification. Those gleefully wielding inflatable bananas in the Anfield away end could thumb their noses. Why not enjoy the dances of defiance until the music stops? The same went for City players, asked to perform under the darkest of clouds, able to focus, at last, on football, rather than legal argument and uncertain futures. Beyond City, the sight of a club found guilty of 100-plus charges laying waste to such rivals as Liverpool was deeply uncomfortable . The Premier League season and product are badly damaged until the matter is somehow resolved. What happened at Anfield should double the haste for a resolution. Chants of “cheat” whenever City players, the game already won, slipped the ball around, are bound to be repeated at other stadiums. Enzo Maresca has described his club’s plight as “noise” but his team’s victory did absolutely nothing to turn the volume down. item.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: Sliding Doors meets Biff’s Almanac: City saga stirs up a world of alternate histories | Max Rushden
item.description: Even New Romantics have a view but this long story will not be cut short amid endless hypotheticals and split narratives It’s Wednesday afternoon (UK time) and I find myself interviewing Tony Hadley on TalkSport about his upcoming big band tour. We play a bit of Spandau Ballet, chat about the classics and his career – hanging out with Frank Sinatra and Tony Bennett. In as much as you can deduce in a 10-minute chat on Zoom, Tony seems like an absolute gent. We do always try to bring it back to sport – Tony is an Arsenal fan, there’s a bit of Arteta, Leeds at the weekend. Tony brings up Billy Bremner and suggests that my co-host Charlie Baker and I are too young to remember him playing. We are, and how wonderful to be called young. Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. Continue reading...

item.title: Mikel Arteta’s new contract reflects where the power now lies at Arsenal | Ed Aarons
item.description: From transfers to stadium works and even the training-ground dog, there is no doubting the Spaniard’s influence at the club If anyone doubts Mikel Arteta’s status as No 1 at Arsenal in the week he committed his future to the club until 2030 , just ask Win the dog. The chocolate labrador who played a starring role in the celebrations when Arsenal were crowned Premier League champions in May has become part of the family at the training ground in Hertfordshire since being introduced by Arteta in May 2023. Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. But, according to sources close to Win, a therapy dog trained not to bark, there is no contest when it comes to her preferred human: Arteta. Continue reading...
